#5288. OpenAI acquires Odessia, travel startup created by Sonder founder

OpenAI has acquired an AI travel agent called Odessia, according to Odessia’s founder, Francis Davidson. Davidson says in a post announcing the deal that he’s now working for OpenAI, helping the AI lab with the future of travel.

Terms of the deal were not disclosed, but this looks like an acqui-hire. Davidson’s announcement focused largely on how he built his AI travel agent Odessia by directing teams of AI agents. The year-old Odessia raised a $6 million pre-seed round led by Sequoia and launched its AI travel agent around five months ago. Davidson says that it had helped early adopters plan millions of dollars’ worth of travel, but the tool has already been shut down.

An OpenAI spokesperson confirmed the hire to TechCrunch. “We’re thrilled to welcome Francis to OpenAI. Francis is a proven founder who has built multiple businesses to help people travel, and we’re excited he’s chosen to build with us.”

However the AI lab has not announced new travel-specific products or plans. It does, however, count such companies as Bookings.com, Expedia, and KAYAK as customers or partners. Travel is also one of the main areas that people are using personal AI assistants to help with. And, back in July 2025, when OpenAI launched its ChatGPT agent, it mentioned travel as one of its potential uses.

OpenAI’s spokesperson didn’t have more to share on its plans for travel-related products, except to say that travel is one of the areas that chatbot users frequently ask about. “1.2 billion people turn to ChatGPT each week for help with everyday tasks — from understanding their health, figuring out what to make for dinner, building a budget, and even planning a trip. We see a real opportunity to make these experiences even more useful,” the spokesperson said.

Acquiring Odessia is interesting for another reason. Davidson is well known in the travel industry after he founded a travel startup called Sonder as a college student in 2014. It was sort of like Airbnb, but it focused on short-term leasing of upscale apartments in major cities worldwide. The pandemic badly hurt it, and as it climbed out of that rut, it went public via a SPAC but didn’t raise as much money as it needed, Davidson later said in a post announcing his resignation as CEO in June 2025.

When a key partnership with Marriott fell through, the company went into bankruptcy and wound down. The bankruptcy trustee sold Sonder’s name, trademarks, and website domain in 2026 to TravelAI, and that website operates as a curated guide to the kind of travel rental properties that Sonder was once known for. Prior to its downfall, Davidson had built Sonder into a unicorn with over $600 million in revenues. While Sonder was not, ultimately, a success story, Davidson is the kind of battle-scarred founder that Silicon Valley often values.

So we’ll have to wait and see what OpenAI has in store with travel now that he’s joined the company.

Note: This story was updated with OpenAI’s comments and updated revenue for Sonder.

CME FedWatch puts the implied chance of a Fed rate hike at 100% for the December 9 meeting, according to the November 12 snapshot. This is another source of pressure on Bitcoin, and there is a good chance the market is going to face its full effect.

Bitcoin and the cryptocurrency market in general aren't set in stone and are highly affected by the performance of traditional markets and the global economy. A rate hike directly affects the desire of investors to expose themselves to riskier assets like crypto.

Bitcoin has been going down rapidly even without the additional source of pressure from the Fed. The current BTC price drop appears to be mostly fueled by insufficient compensation for the risk: Bitcoin and crypto in general aren't as attractive as tech or AI stocks, so it is far better to get exposed to the latter ones.

That is the bearish reading here. FedWatch reflects futures pricing, so the hike is already expected rather than guaranteed to become a fresh shock.

Bitcoin is trading at $72,744, below all the moving averages shown on the daily chart. A drop below $70,000 shouldn't necessarily trigger any substantial surge of selling pressure, considering how stretched the decline already looks.

The imbalance of inflows and outflows is still staggering in this reading of the market. The concern is that almost every top-15 crypto asset remains in endurance mode, facing persistent outflows fueled by security concerns, a retreat in investor sentiment and a lack of substantial recovery prospects.

#5286. With $720M round, Britain’s Fractile gets a leg up in the race for AI chips

Fractile, a British startup developing AI chips, has raised a $720 million Series C backed by Britain’s Sovereign AI Fund with hopes of “ensuring the U.K. has a greater stake in the hardware that will underpin its future economy,” its government stated.

Alongside the likes of Axelera, Etched, and OLIX, this makes Fractile one of the top-funded startup players in the race for purpose-built AI chips. Such chips are one of several avenues being explored to reduce the cost of inference — aka using increasingly demanding AI models in production.

However, Fractile seeks to go beyond hardware with a full-stack approach that also includes a machine learning compiler to maximize the speed at which LLMs will get executed on its chips.

As a result, the company frames itself as a frontier AI company, and its latest round led by Thrive Capital, Founders Fund, Lightspeed Venture Partners, and Redpoint was priced accordingly. According to the British government, the valuation was “over £5 billion” — quite possibly $7 billion, a figure reported both by the Financial Times and a Reuters source.

Still, Fractile’s main differentiator will arguably be its hardware design. After a pivot, its approach now revolves on DRAM, the most common type of RAM, but stacked on top of each chip in such a way that it is hoping will bypass the usual trade-off between memory and capacity.

This trade-off has become more problematic with the rise of agentic AI, as companies seek to perform longer chains of tasks with large models without compromising on speed. As compute struggles to keep up, hopes are high for AI chips, despite their limited availability to date.

In a LinkedIn post, Fractile CEO Walter Goodwin wrote that “there is still a lot of work ahead” for the company, and that the new funding will enable the startup to “ship [its] first chips and systems next year.”

#5285. Nine Korean startups vie for a spot in Disrupt 2027’s Startup Battlefield 200 competition

TechCrunch’s yearly Startup Battlefield 200 competition sees hundreds of companies from across the world trying every year to get a chance to pitch in front of VCs and the international tech community at the TechCrunch Disrupt conference.

This week, nine early-stage South Korean startups pitched at DETO 2026, a technology conference in Seoul, to earn a spot in next year’s Startup Battlefield 200.

The startups work across the deep tech sector, including healthcare, fintech, energy, semiconductors, and AI. All nine startups are looking to enter the U.S. market as part of the broader international expansion plans.

Voinosis, which develops AI to detect changes in brain health through voice analysis, won the competition. The other eight startups are listed below in alphabetical order.

Voinosis is developing an AI tool that analyzes speech patterns such as pitch, pauses, rhythm, and response times to detect changes linked to brain health. Each voice check takes less than five minutes.

The company says its technology has been tested in Greek, Japanese, and English, and its product doesn’t require separate training for each language. In a clinical study involving 146 participants, the startup claims its tech achieved 88% accuracy in screening for potential cognitive issues.

Voinosis targets hospitals, senior living facilities, insurers, and individual consumers. It also plans to link voice checks with cognitive training, assessments, and treatment provided by healthcare professionals.

The startup was founded by Grace Shin, who spent more than 25 years as an otologic surgeon. The startup is currently raising a Series A round and has already secured a South Korean pharmaceutical company as a strategic investor.

Awesome Lab, based in Seoul, makes ThermoFlux, a heating system that uses water electrolysis and ionization to generate heat. The system can manage heat production for buildings, water supply, and industrial processes. The company says its technology can reduce energy consumption and carbon emissions.

For its international expansion, Awesome Lab is taking a different approach in each market. In the U.S., it plans to supply core OEM modules and work with boiler, water heater, and HVAC companies on product development.

Crosshub helps travelers and international visitors verify their identities and set up payment methods abroad. Its platform, IDBlock, combines identity verification and payment services using self-sovereign identity (SSI) and zero-knowledge proof.

The company says its platform helps users prove their identity across borders without sharing unnecessary personal information. Crosshub is also integrating this technology with payment systems to improve access to financial services for travelers.

DeepFusion AI has developed a 4D radar-based imaging system with additional sensors for autonomous mobility, robotaxi, maritime surveillance, and defense applications. The system combines RF sensors with radar and lidar to detect objects, movement, or distance without a direct line of sight. All sensors are supposedly packed into a single, customizable unit.

EFLOW develops special motors that can produce more torque, or rotational force, while taking up less space for use in robots, drones, satellites, and other mobility applications. The startup also develops actuators that control how robotic joints move.

Otiton Medical makes two medical devices: One specializes in measuring body temperature, while another can capture ear canal images and analyze the eardrum. The company says its AI was trained on about 55,000 images of eardrums, and the device has received medical certification in South Korea.

Riibotics says it can deploy robots into warehouses within a day. Riibotics wants to reduce deployment costs for warehouses by streamlining setup, which includes infrastructure setup, warehouse mapping, system integration through custom middleware, task programming, and safety checks.

Ternell, a semiconductor startup based in Ulsan, is developing a new type of memory to help AI chips use less power.

Unlike conventional two-state memory, Ternell’s T-SRAM system adds a third state for more efficient data storage. Founded in 2019 by KyungRok Kim, a former Samsung Electronics engineer, Ternell reports that tests with 28-nanometer chips showed a 33% to 102% increase in memory capacity per area, and a 55% to 71% reduction in energy needed to access data, compared with conventional SRAM.

Testbank is a Korean edtech startup developing Solve, an app that converts printed study materials, such as workbooks and test-prep books, into interactive digital versions.

The startup uses AI to identify question and answer spaces in publishers’ PDF files while preserving the original layout. Solve lets you write answers directly on the page and be graded automatically.

#5284. XRP Risks Losing $1 Amid Aggressive $2.5 Billion Shift

As XRP continues to struggle amid the broad crypto market volatility while failing in multiple attempts to recover, key on-chain metrics are pointing to increased selling pressure among traders.

While momentum remains extremely weak, latest data from crypto analytics platform, Cryptoquant, shows that sellers have dominated both XRP’s spot and futures markets, putting it at risk of losing the long-held $1 mark.

Per the data, XRP’s cumulative volume delta (CVD) across major cryptocurrency exchanges shows that aggressive selling has dominated both its spot and futures market since September 23.

As of November 12, XRP’s Perpetual CVD on Binance has fallen from -$109 million to about -$1.1 billion. It is important to note that the CVD of an asset is a key metric that measures the difference between the volume of aggressive buy orders and aggressive sell orders over time.

While the metric turns negative when more traders are aggressively selling than buying, the -991 million negative balance in the Binance perpetual CVD signals stronger selling pressure.

With the negative balance on Binance exceeding its previous level by more than 10 times, this shows that traders have placed significantly more market sell orders than buy orders, either by opening short positions or closing existing long positions.

Apart from its futures market, further data shows that sellers have also dominated XRP’s spot activity across all major crypto exchanges, including Binance.

Notably, XRP’s All CEX Estimated Spot CVD moved from -$400 million to -$2.9 billion over the same period.

While this marks a $2.5 billion increase in the imbalance favoring sellers, it indicates that XRP spot traders have also been selling XRP more aggressively rather than buying, propelling the asset for further price declines.

#5283. Nanbeige4.3-33B Ties Qwen3.8-27B on Intelligence Index, but Spends 44% More Output Tokens

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

Nanbeige4.3-33B matches Qwen3.8-27B at 20 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index but uses 158K output tokens per task against 110K. Here is what that costs locally.

Two models just posted the same score. One needed 158,000 output tokens per task to get there. The other needed 110,000.

Nanbeige4.3-33B, a dense 33-billion-parameter reasoning model from the foundation model team at BOSS Zhipin, scores 20 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5. According to Artificial Analysis's evaluation, published November 5, that matches Qwen3.8 27B at its xhigh reasoning setting. The model is open weights under Apache 2.0, accepts text only, and has a 524K-token context window.

Behind the tie sits a gap in effort. Artificial Analysis says Nanbeige used 158K output tokens per Intelligence Index task against 110K for Qwen3.8 27B, about 44% more. That weighted average covers answer and reasoning tokens across all nine v5 evaluations, including agentic tool-use turns. For anyone running these models, tokens translate into time, electricity or money, so the same score doesn't mean the same cost.

The Intelligence Index v5 combines nine evaluations, among them AA-Briefcase, AutomationBench-AA, Terminal-Bench 4.0, FrontierCode 2.0 and AA-Omniscience. A score of 20 puts Nanbeige well above the 6 of Muse Glimmer, a 30B model in the same comparison. Artificial Analysis also notes that Nanbeige sets a new Pareto-optimal point for Intelligence Index against total parameters, since both it and Qwen3.8 27B are dense models. A larger mixture-of-experts model like DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, by contrast, scores 33 while activating only 16B parameters per token.

The model card Nanbeige's lab published on Hugging Face describes the base model, positioned as the flagship teacher for the Nanbeige4.3 series. The lab says it will distill agentic capabilities into smaller models, such as an upcoming 3B version. On base-model benchmarks, the card shows 66.9 on MMLU-Pro against 59.3 for Gemma4-31B-Base. Those figures belong to the base model and are separate from the reasoning model's Intelligence Index result.

The two models reach 20 by different routes. Nanbeige scores 30% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 against 6% for Qwen, and 16% on the CritPt v2 Hard Subset against 4%. It also edges Qwen on AutomationBench-AA, 53% to 48%.

Elsewhere, it falls behind. On AA-Briefcase v1.1 it scores 1162 Elo against 1391, on FrontierCode 2.0 11% against 15%, and on HLE-Diamond 7% against 15%. The knowledge test tells the most distinctive story. On AA-Omniscience v1.1, Nanbeige scores -4 against Qwen's -6, with an 18% hallucination rate against 29%. Yet it answers only 29% of questions against 43%, declines 71% of them and gets 12% correct against 17%.

For general question answering, Qwen's higher accuracy is the better result.

Output tokens aren't a vanity metric. A reasoning model writes out its thinking as tokens, and every one costs decode time. If both models ran at the same speed on the same hardware, Nanbeige would take about 44% longer to finish a typical task.

Local decoding adds a second factor. Generation is usually limited by memory bandwidth, because each new token requires reading the model's weights, and a 33B dense model reads about 20% more weight data per token than a 27B dense model. Assuming the same quantization and the same memory-bound hardware, those two effects compound to roughly 1.7 times the wall-clock time per task. That figure is a back-of-the-envelope calculation, not a measured result.

Nor is there a hosted alternative to soften the blow. Artificial Analysis lists no confirmed public first-party or third-party APIs for Nanbeige, so unlike Qwen, which is sold per token through Alibaba's API, the cost is the hardware you run it on and the time it takes.

Artificial Analysis describes the model as small enough to run locally on a laptop, which holds true with a caveat. The weights are published in BF16, which at 33 billion parameters means roughly 66 GB, far beyond almost any laptop. At 8-bit, the weights fall to about 33 GB, and at 4-bit to about 17 GB, plus memory for the context cache. A machine with 24 GB of unified memory or more can plausibly hold a 4-bit build, though a long context will push it.

The vendor's own quickstart points the other way. The card's SGLang and vLLM examples both set tensor parallelism across four GPUs, which suggests the reference deployment is a multi-GPU server. Its Transformers example also enables trust_remote_code=True, which runs code from the repository. Reading that code first is the safer move, as is serving the model through vLLM or SGLang instead.

Quantization changes the model, too. The Intelligence Index numbers come from Artificial Analysis's own runs, so a 4-bit local build may score somewhat lower, or generate different token counts, than the version they evaluated.

This release is a clean example of why a headline score isn't enough. Nanbeige delivers Qwen-level results at 33B, with strengths in terminal tasks and physics reasoning and a more cautious answering style. The price for those strengths is length.

Anyone choosing between the two should run both on their own workload and record three numbers: the score on their tasks, output tokens per task and seconds per task on their hardware. For terminal-heavy, agentic work, Nanbeige's profile may justify the longer runs. For knowledge-heavy or latency-sensitive work, Qwen's shorter, more accurate answers look stronger.

Three signals are worth watching next: whether the 3B distilled version keeps the model's strengths, whether other labs report the same token behavior, and whether anyone publishes quantized local benchmarks. Until then, the simplest summary is also the most accurate: same score, different bill.

#5282. Phota Labs uses AI to turn everyday photos into professional-looking shots

A new iOS app called Phota Labs gives users access to a personal AI photo assistant that turns everyday snapshots into images that look like they were taken by a professional photographer, all while preserving the authenticity of the image.

Rather than giving consumers yet another photo-editing tool, Phota Labs aims to use advances in AI to automate the editing process so it’s easier for anyone to get access to better photos.

The a16z-backed startup was founded by Cecilia Zhang and Zach Xia, who met at Adobe while working on computational photography products, including Project Indigo, Lightroom, and Photoshop.

The duo saw a gap in the editing tools on the market and believed that although editing tools can be powerful for enhancing photos, they aren’t very effective at fixing a photo that wasn’t captured well in the first place. Phota Labs changes that by focusing on fixing the shot itself while preserving the natural appearances of those in the image.

“Phota is your personal photo assistant that can make great photos for any moment you want to keep before you even ask, which means that it’s a very proactive experience,” Zhang told TechCrunch in an interview. “Think of it almost like a photographer or virtual photographer who looks over your camera roll and tries to understand what’s happening and how they could have taken that photo for you on the spot for that scene.”

The idea is to use AI to transform photos, whether that’s turning a wide-angle group photo into a tighter portrait or transforming a selfie into a regular shot.

Users can choose from different photography styles that determine how AI transforms their images, ranging from subtle edits that preserve the original lens and composition to more dramatic transformations that introduce effects like fish-eye lenses, alternative angles, and entirely different perspectives.

While some people turn to ChatGPT and other generative AI tools to enhance or edit images, these tools can often alter a person’s appearance, especially when working with blurry photos because they don’t know what that person actually looks like.

“For Phota, we built our own tech,” Zhang said. ”We built this personalization technology that actually learns about people’s identity and is able to preserve them in any transformation we do to a photo.”

Images edited with Phota Labs feature invisible watermarks that identify them as altered by AI when shared on social platforms.

The startup is initially targeting people who take tons of photos and like to share them on social media, but don’t want to deal with the tedious process of editing photos. Over time, the founders envision a broader audience, from retirees looking to create beautiful photos for their grandchildren to parents who want to share polished family albums with friends and relatives.

“We have this obsession with authenticity,” Xia said. “I think there’s so much value in connecting AI with real moments and making sure those photos are not perfect, in a sense. That’s why we spend a lot of research into understanding personal context, into building this identity model because we want to make sure the photos are authentic. They’re just better photos of the same moment, rather than saying, ‘Oh, this is an AI image’.”

Xia said beta users were excited to see better versions of moments they had actually lived and saw the results as photos of real memories rather than AI-generated images. The founders discovered that users were taking more photos because they knew Phota Labs could enhance them later.

“We’re turning something that’s unusable into something that people want to print,” Zhang said. “People who just love photos but never really got into editing can now experience professional quality that could never have been possible. So, I think that meant so much to us. There’s so many cherished moments for photos, and we really want them to be actually meaningful and something that you can remember.”

In terms of funding, the company raised a $5.6 million seed round led by a16z last year.

Phota Labs is launching as a free app to build an initial user base before exploring a freemium model. The startup also plans to launch an Android app in the future.

F2Pool co-founder Chun Wang, known on X as Satofishi, bought 5,246 ETH worth $10.78 million over the past two days at an average price of $2,054, according to Lookonchain and Arkham data.

On Nov. 5, with ether trading near $2,400, Wang sold 6,200 wrapped staked ETH (wstETH) for $18.5 million in USDC. Wrapped staked ETH is a version of Lido's staked ether (stETH) that can be used in DeFi protocols.

This week, ether traded about 14% lower than on the day of the sale, and Wang started buying it back.

He withdrew 5,246 ETH from Binance hot wallets in two transfers of 3,996 ETH and 1,250 ETH. The purchase cost him $10.78 million, so about $7.7 million from the Nov. 5 sale is still left in USDC, according to Lookonchain.

Wang then sent 3,996 ETH ($8.23 million) to Lido. Lido is the largest liquid staking protocol on Ethereum. He deposited the wstETH he received into Spark, a lending protocol in the Sky ecosystem, which was previously known as MakerDAO. In Spark, wstETH can be used as collateral, while it continues to earn staking rewards.

He started out arbitraging Bitcoin between overseas exchanges and China's Taobao and later co-founded F2Pool. He launched the pool in 2013 together with Mao Shixing. At that time, F2Pool was one of the first Bitcoin mining pools in China.

In 2015, he bought a condo in Pattaya for 2,900 BTC. He later sold it for 7 BTC, as the price of Bitcoin had risen many times over.

In 2025, Wang also funded and commanded Fram2, the first crewed spaceflight over Earth's polar regions, on a SpaceX Crew Dragon.

F2Pool also mined ether until Ethereum moved to proof-of-stake in September 2022. Before that, Wang launched the non-custodial staking service stakefish. According to Wang, he decided to do it after a conversation with Vitalik Buterin in 2017. Stakefish was also one of the first node operators of Lido.

Ether is down more than 15% since the start of the month amid outflows from spot ETFs, according to SoSoValue. At press time, ETH is trading at $2,020.

The Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation (DTCC) will connect its tokenization service to Solana (SOL) in the second half of 2027, the company said on Nov. 12.

The integration will allow "digital twins" of Russell 1000 stocks, major ETFs and U.S. Treasuries to be issued on the Solana blockchain. In December 2025, the SEC issued a no-action letter that allowed DTC to tokenize these assets.

In 2025, DTCC processed $4.7 quadrillion in securities transactions. Its depository, DTC, holds and services $114 trillion in assets from more than 150 countries.

The DTCC Tokenization Service (DTS) will let large market participants convert conventional securities into tokens, move them across the Solana network and redeem them.

"DTC-tokenized assets made available on Solana – and all blockchain networks integrated with the service – will retain the same investor protections, ownership rights and regulatory safeguards that apply to traditionally held securities," said Brian Steele, president of DTCC Clearing & Securities Services.

According to DTCC CEO Frank La Salla, the integration will also free up securities for use as collateral.

DTS went live on Oct. 28, 2026. At launch, it worked with Canton Network and a private ledger. DTCC said that it adds new networks at clients' request.

"DTCC is committed to providing an open and connected platform that provides our users with access to mature distributed ledger technology networks like Solana that have established performance, security and governance features," said Nadine Chakar, global head of DTCC Digital Assets.

Nick Ducoff, general manager for institutional at the Solana Foundation, also commented on the news. "Institutions choose Solana because it already runs real financial activity at scale," he said.

According to Ducoff, the integration "connects one of the most trusted names in post-trade infrastructure with a network built for always-on markets."

As of Nov. 12, distributed real-world assets (RWA) in the Solana ecosystem reached $5.13 billion across more than 1.02 million holders, according to RWA.xyz. Transfers over the past 30 days totaled $16.48 billion.

The stablecoin market cap on Solana stands at $13.85 billion, with monthly turnover of $387.41 billion.

Decentralized exchange Hyperliquid has bought back and burned 21,200 HYPE over the past 24 hours, spending $1.53 million on the purchase at an average price of $72.31, according to Onchain Lens.

The on-chain analytics platform also reported that Hyperliquid has permanently removed a total of 50.47 million HYPE from circulation since the launch of the token. That is 5.05% of the max supply of 1 billion HYPE, and at the current price, the burned tokens are worth around $3.51 billion.

The latest buyback comes amid the decline in the price of the cryptocurrency. On Nov. 12, the price of HYPE went down by 3.45%, and at press time, the token stands at $69.52, according to TradingView. Earlier this autumn, the price of HYPE was above $90.

Hyperliquid pays for the buybacks in dollars, so the decentralized exchange is able to buy more HYPE with the same amount of money when the price of the token goes down.

DeFiLlama data shows that Hyperliquid has earned $1.41 billion for HYPE holders since December 2024. Over the past 30 days, the decentralized exchange earned $68.82 million, and its earnings for the past week stand at $15.04 million.

Over the last day, the platform collected about $1.46 million in fees, slightly less than the amount it spent on the buyback. Besides, DeFiLlama data shows that Hyperliquid currently earns more in fees than Ethereum, Tron and Base.

The largest part of the burned tokens, 48.85 million HYPE, was bought back by the Assistance Fund. The fund automatically receives between 97% and 99% of the fees from perpetual and spot trading on Hyperliquid, and the rest of the fees go to the HLP liquidity pool and to the builders of individual markets.

The Assistance Fund buys HYPE on the open market and sends the tokens to the "0xfefe...fefe" address. It is a system address that does not have a private key. In December 2025, Hyperliquid validators formally recognized the tokens held at this address as burned.

In August 2026, Hyperliquid also introduced the AQAv2 upgrade. Under the upgrade, around 90% of the yield generated by the USDC reserves on the platform now goes to the Assistance Fund. Each of these transfers brings between $14 million and $16 million to the fund.

Besides the Assistance Fund, HYPE is also burned through network fees. Around 1.24 million HYPE has been burned through fees and slashing on HyperCore, the base layer of Hyperliquid. Another 376,060 HYPE has been burned as gas fees on HyperEVM, the smart contract layer of the network.

#5277. Five Forged Receipts Drained $304.5K From Ankr's Ethereum Bridge Using a 0.0044 ankrETH Deposit

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

SlowMist says five forged receipts with valid signatures let an attacker drain about $304,500 from Ankr's Ethereum bridge using one old Optimism deposit. Here is how the check failed.Every one of the five receipts was signed by the bridge's own trusted signer. Every one pointed to a deposit that had already been paid out.

On November 9, an attacker drained about $304,500 from Ankr's Ethereum cross-chain bridge. According to SlowMist's alert, the attacker built five forged receipts that all referenced a single legitimate Optimism transaction, changing the recipient, the token and the withdrawal amount in each one.

All five carried valid signatures from the bridge's trusted consensus signer.

The reused transaction was tiny: a deposit of about 0.0044 ankrETH made on Optimism on November 3, which SlowMist's analysis says had already been redeemed on Ethereum the same day. Six days later, that one settled deposit was cited five times. The incident is recorded in the SlowMist Hacked database.Blockaid flagged the exploit as it unfolded, at about 08:42 UTC, with roughly $292,000 already gone. SlowMist followed at 09:14 UTC with the higher $304,500 estimate and an explanation of the forged receipts. Ankr paused withdrawals, and no recovery plan has been confirmed.

The design is common across lock-and-release bridges. A user deposits on the source chain, and an off-chain set of signers watches for that deposit and signs a receipt describing it. The destination contract, in this case Ankr's Ethereum bridge contract, checks that the receipt carries a valid signature and then releases the funds.That setup makes the signers the source of truth. The contract can't see Optimism, so it leans on the signature to prove the deposit happened. The weak point sits in the gap between "the signer signed this" and "this really happened." A contract that treats the first as proof of the second inherits every mistake the signing process makes.

SlowMist's finding is precise: the withdrawal function released assets without independently verifying the actual event on the source chain. A signature confirmed that the signer approved a message. It did not confirm that the message matched a deposit that existed, that was still unused, and that involved the same recipient, token and amount.The replay angle deserves attention, even though SlowMist's summary only implies it. A bridge normally marks each source event as consumed, keyed to something fixed like the source chain, transaction hash and log index, so it can be paid out once. If replay protection keys on the contents of the receipt instead, changing the recipient, token or amount produces a receipt the contract has never seen. Five edited receipts against one deposit would then look like five fresh claims. That is one plausible way the pieces fit together, not a finding the researchers have published.Bridge history offers parallels. In 2022, Wormhole lost about $325 million when an attacker got a forged message past its signature verification, and Nomad lost about $190 million after a misconfiguration let nearly any message pass as valid. The Ankr case is smaller, but it shares the same root: the verification step accepted something it shouldn't have.

The Ethereum transactions show the attacker extracted about 82.91 ankrETH, 515,206 ankrPOL and 7.98 million ANKR tokens. Blockaid described the five withdraw calls as using the tiny Optimism deposit to unlock the bridge's locked inventory and send it to a new wallet.The mix of assets tells its own story. Each forged receipt named a different token and amount, which suggests the attacker picked targets based on what the bridge held. That fits receipts built entirely by the attacker, apart from the one real transaction reference. Anyone wanting to trace them can open the bridge contract's transaction list on Etherscan and filter for the five `withdraw` calls on November 9.

The most important fact is still missing. SlowMist says the origin of the unauthorized signatures is under investigation, and it hasn't confirmed whether the signers were compromised.A valid signature on a forged receipt has a short list of explanations. A signing key, or the service holding it, could have been accessed. A signing service could have been tricked into signing attacker-supplied data. Or the signing logic itself could have a flaw that produces signatures for receipts it shouldn't. Each one points to a different fix: a stolen key means rotating signers, a manipulated service means tightening input validation off-chain, and a logic flaw means rewriting the signing rules.Whichever it turns out to be, the on-chain contract and the off-chain signer both failed to ask the same question. Either one verifying the source event would likely have stopped the attack, and neither did.

The lessons are narrow and practical. Replay protection should key on the immutable identity of the source event, not on the receipt's contents, and a source event should be consumable exactly once. The destination contract should confirm that the receipt's recipient, token and amount match what the source-chain event actually recorded, using a proof or an independent verifier instead of trusting the signer alone.Signer infrastructure needs its own scrutiny. Threshold schemes, hardware-backed keys and strict limits on what a signing service will sign all shrink the damage from a single failure. Rate limits and per-withdrawal caps help as well. A bridge that can release its entire locked inventory in five calls has no brake once a signature check is defeated.Trust in a bridge comes in layers, and one layer rarely holds up alone. Users with funds in Ankr's bridge should watch for the project's post-mortem and its plan for restoring withdrawals. For developers, the question to put to their own code is a blunt one: if a signer signs something false, what stops the contract from believing it?

#5276. MSCI Drops Saylor's Strategy From Its Index Amid BTC Sell-Off

MSCI has published the results of its November 2026 Index Review, with Strategy among the companies set to leave the MSCI USA Index.

Metaplanet, the Tokyo-listed Bitcoin treasury company, is also scheduled for removal from the MSCI Japan Small Cap Index.

The changes will take effect after the market close on November 30, 2026.

Across the MSCI ACWI Index, 13 securities will be added and 100 deleted. The two additions to the MSCI World Index, measured by full company market capitalization, are Moderna (USA) and Aritzia (Canada).

The latest review follows the new rules proposed by MSCI in October, among which are new measures regarding crypto treasury holding companies.

MSCI evaluates whether a company maintains substantial operating assets and applies five financial ratio tests. In case a company fails to meet at least four criteria,

A company that fails at least four criteria across consecutive annual reporting periods may face removal from the MSCI Global Investable Market Indexes.

MSCI indexes track public companies based on market cap and investment risks. Global mutual funds and ETFs use these benchmarks to build their portfolios.

Dropping out of such index could influence investment flows as well as stock prices.

Strategy continues to accumulate BTC despite the crypto market staying in red zone.

Between November 2 and November 8, 2026, the company acquired another 1,036 BTC at an average price of $79,012.

As of November 12, Strategy holds 850,364 BTC. The company also reported about $5.5 billion in USD reserves.

However, Bitcoin's recent decline below $75,000 pushes Strategy's holdings into an unrealized loss of $500 million.

Strategy's stock (MSTR) fell 7% on Thursday, while Bitcoin is down 3.5% at the time of writing.

Microsoft stock has another problem beyond its latest global outage. While the disruption to Outlook, Teams and Copilot has put cloud reliability under scrutiny, the company’s aggressive AI infrastructure spending is creating a separate challenge for investors. Microsoft is growing rapidly, but sustaining that momentum requires enormous capital commitments. With MSFT approaching a key technical resistance zone, investors have more than one risk to assess.

Microsoft’s latest global outage has exposed the risks of its growing dependence on cloud-based workplace services. The disruption, which began on November 12, affected Outlook, Exchange Online, Teams, SharePoint and Copilot across multiple regions.

BREAKING: Microsoft's Outlook, Teams and Copilot have been down for over 15 hours.Microsoft says it's not a cyberattack, but servers going down unexpectedly.$MSFT is down -3% in premarket. pic.twitter.com/o4xpAG8e2F

The incident lasted more than 12 hours, disrupting businesses, government agencies and other organizations. Microsoft attributed the problem to server and infrastructure issues and said it had found no indication of malicious activity. Its recovery efforts initially struggled as some restored servers became unresponsive under returning traffic.

The disruption also follows another Microsoft 365 service incident earlier this year, bringing reliability concerns back into focus. For enterprise customers, consistent uptime is central to Microsoft’s competitive position. Repeated failures could encourage large organizations to reconsider their dependence on a single cloud ecosystem.

The immediate financial damage remains unclear, but the reputational risk is harder to measure. Investors will be watching Microsoft’s post-incident explanation and whether the company can demonstrate that its infrastructure is becoming more resilient.

The second concern is the scale of Microsoft’s AI investment. The company is expanding data-center capacity to support Azure, AI workloads and growing demand for computing infrastructure. Microsoft reported $45.2 billion in capital expenditure for fiscal Q1 2027, while management expects calendar-year 2026 spending to reach approximately $170 billion. It also indicated that quarterly capital expenditure could exceed $50 billion in the December quarter.

The investment is supported by strong demand. Azure revenue increased 48% in the September quarter, while Microsoft Cloud revenue rose 30% to $63.9 billion. Commercial remaining performance obligations also climbed 73% to $677 billion.

However, the central question is how quickly that demand translates into returns. Heavy infrastructure spending can pressure free cash flow and operating margins, particularly when new capacity takes time to become productive.

Microsoft’s own filings warn that slower AI adoption, underutilized infrastructure and rising computing costs could affect future returns. The company is therefore facing a demanding balance: invest enough to capture AI growth without allowing capital costs to outrun revenue generation.

Microsoft’s cloud business remains a major strength, but sustaining its current growth rate will not be straightforward. Azure grew 48% in the latest quarter, and management expects growth of 49% to 50% in constant currency for the December quarter. However, Microsoft also acknowledged that customer demand continues to exceed available supply, while some third-party GPU capacity deliveries have been delayed.

Microsoft stock price closed at $539.44 on November 13, gaining 1.08%. The stock is approaching a major supply zone between $550 and $560, where previous advances have encountered selling pressure. A sustained breakout above this region could strengthen the recovery and bring $575 into focus.

On the downside, $515 is the immediate support area, followed by $490â$500. The broader demand zone sits around $375â$390, although that remains well below the current trading range. The moving averages continue to provide support beneath the current price, but the recent rejection near the supply zone suggests buyers have yet to establish control. A breakout above $560 would improve the technical outlook, while a decline below $515 could weaken the recovery.

Microsoft’s long-term growth story remains supported by Azure expansion, enterprise software and AI demand. However, the latest outage has highlighted operational risks, while the company’s infrastructure spending raises questions about capital efficiency and future profitability.

The next phase will depend on whether Microsoft can restore customer confidence, convert AI demand into sustainable revenue and maintain cloud growth without sacrificing margins.

#5274. XRP, SHIB, BTC and Other Tokens Hit Hard by Abrupt Resignation of Nvidia CEO

Top digital assets like Bitcoin (BTC), XRP, Ethereum (ETH) and Shiba Inu (SHIB) are facing heavy selling pressure following a severe setback in the crypto market after the sudden exit of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.

The unexpected exit of the Nvidia co-founder has created pandemonium in the financial world as shares of the artificial intelligence company have been hit by a heavy sell-off, further straining an already weak crypto market.

According to reports by Reuters, Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang resigned on Nov. 12. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress has taken over as interim chief executive.

There are controversies surrounding Huang's personal life and doubts about his future at the company he co-founded over three decades ago.

The news of Huang's exit has triggered a heavy sell-off in Nvidia stock, with shares dropping over 12% in early trading, wiping out an estimated $500 billion in market value.

The sell-off has also affected crypto-related trading markets.

As recently revealed by blockchain analytics platform Lookonchain, a trader known as 0x7368 had his leveraged long position in Nvidia stock fully liquidated.

According to Lookonchain, the trader had 9,959 units of Nvidia (NVDA), worth about $1.54 million, liquidated after news of Jensen Huang's resignation hit the market.

Kitao answered in English. Most of his recent posts on X are in Japanese, and the rest of them are reposts of other accounts.

Kitao previously worked as an executive at Nomura Securities and later served as CFO of SoftBank. In 1999, he founded SoftBank Investment, which later became SBI Holdings. Today, SBI includes banks, brokerage, and insurance businesses, as well as crypto services.

The partnership began in 2016. SBI joined Ripple's Series B round and launched a joint venture with Ripple, SBI Ripple Asia. SBI owns about 60% of the venture, and Ripple owns the remaining 40%.

In 2018, SBI launched the interbank app MoneyTap. The same year, SBI's crypto exchange, now called SBI VC Trade, started operations with XRP trading. In 2019, Kitao joined Ripple's board of directors.

From 2020, SBI began handing the token out to shareholders as bonuses, and the payment service SBI Remit launched remittances using it with on-demand liquidity (ODL), including in the major Japan-Philippines corridor.

SBI kept working with Ripple during the SEC lawsuit against the company, which lasted from December 2020 until 2025.

Back on February 15, 2026, in rare long-form tweets in English, Kitao denied rumors that SBI holds $10 billion worth of XRP: "Not $10 billion in XRP, but around 9% of Ripple Labs. So our hidden asset could be much bigger." By his account, the combined valuation of Ripple Labs and its ecosystem is "enormous," and SBI owns more than 9% of all of it.

Kitao also talked about XRP at SBI's quarterly briefing on November 2, 2026. He said that investors buy Bitcoin mostly to hold it, and that the value of XRP depends on its use in payments and business ecosystems.

In August 2025, SBI VC Trade and Ripple agreed to bring the RLUSD stablecoin to Japan. In October 2025, SBI also invested $200 million in Evernorth, a company that holds XRP in its treasury. By now, SBI VC Trade has more than two million accounts.

#5270. Pompliano Says Bitcoin Spot ETFs Are Safer and More Convenient Than Hardware Wallets for Bitcoiners Holding Over $10,000

Pompliano’s comments on Bitcoin hardware wallets and Bitcoin ETFs come at a time when more people show interest in BTC amid security threats.

Bitcoin expert Anthony Pompliano today tackled a crucial question that serious Bitcoin investors often ask. The question is: between hardware wallets and ETFs, which one offers the best outcome for securing and getting exposure to Bitcoin?

In an interview released early today, the celebrated crypto analyst answered questions savvy investors want answered about Bitcoin self-custody versus Bitcoin ETFs.

Today, Bitcoin adoption grows at a remarkable rate. As more investors seek to invest in the cryptocurrency, there are two major ways to do so: gaining exposure through Bitcoin hardware wallets (self-custody) or Bitcoin ETFs.

In the podcast, Pompliano admitted that using spot ETFs is more secure than storing Bitcoin in a hardware wallet. According to the crypto expert, spot ETFs offer an accessible approach, providing investors with a simplified, regulated way to buy and invest in Bitcoin through their existing brokerage accounts. As Pompliano stated, ETFs stand out because they emphasize the importance of regulation in providing investor protection and market integrity.

Pompliano further recognized spot ETFs as the safest and the most convenient option for investors holding between $10,000 and $10 million worth of BTC. He said these investment vehicles offer greater liquidity than directly holding BTC on hardware wallets. They provide investors with diversified exposure to stock exchanges and on-chain markets.

However, he said convenience comes with caveats, as ETFs provide indirect exposure to Bitcoin. This means that investors don’t actually own the underlying Bitcoin. Also, ETFs might not provide investors with the same level of control as directly owning BTC in self-custody wallets.

This highlights the advantages of Bitcoin hardware wallets, which allow customers to hold BTC directly, giving them greater control. However, this level of control comes with the responsibility of managing private keys, asset control, and security risks.

The debate between self-custody and ETFs comes at a time when the crypto industry continues to experience increasing security breaches, with the latest and largest one being the Binance infiltration.

Such unfortunate hacking events compel customers to rethink how to secure their BTC while still accessing strong liquidity. The self-custody approach offers direct ownership and control of BTC, though it requires technical know-how and involves greater security risks. On the other hand, ETFs offer a simple, regulated way to gain exposure to the asset, with diversified liquidity. They, however, come with some limitations.

#5266. How Bittensor's Gamma Turns Every AI Payment Into an Alpha Burn

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

Paying a Bittensor subnet with gamma burns its alpha token. Here is how gamma gets minted, how the lower-price rule works and why the credit can never be converted back.Pay a Bittensor subnet for an AI answer with gamma, and your payment vanishes. The alpha token behind it gets burned, the credit gets spent, and nobody can redeem either one.

Using a subnet's service today usually means creating an account, adding funds and collecting an API key, and every additional subnet repeats the routine. Opentensor announced gamma to cut that friction. With gamma, a Bittensor wallet handles both access and payment across any subnet that adopts the standard.The mechanics are laid out in the gamma guide in the subtensor docs. Gamma is a credit a subnet can accept as payment, valued in US dollars. A customer gets it by burning that subnet's alpha token, and each dollar of burned alpha value mints one gamma, so a burn valued at $100 creates 100 gamma.Each balance stays tied to the subnet where it was created. Gamma minted for subnet 51 can't pay for a service on any other subnet. Root switches the system on network-wide, and each subnet owner or lease beneficiary then enables it for their own subnet.

Customers have two ways in. They can pay with TAO, and the protocol buys the subnet’s alpha and burns it in a single transaction. Or they can pay with alpha they already hold on that subnet, and the protocol burns it directly to create gamma.

Setup takes four steps. The customer creates a fresh hotkey that will act as an API key, associates it with their coldkey, looks up the service they want and mints. The docs give the command: btcli gamma mint --netuid 51 --hotkey API_KEY --amount-tao 10 --service-hotkey SERVICE_HOTKEY. The TAO route follows the same pool and flow accounting as stake-burn and creates no stake position. Users who hold stake can burn it with mint-gamma-with-stake, and --amount-alpha all burns the whole position.

The gamma lands in a deposit. Each deposit belongs to the minting coldkey and is keyed by the API-key hotkey, which signs the customer's requests. A hotkey holds at most one deposit per subnet, and a coldkey holds at most 64 per subnet. The docs warn against reusing a staking hotkey or a coldkey, because requests signed with the key get paid from the deposit.A few guardrails apply. A mint must reach at least 0.1 gamma. By default, the SDK quotes the mint first and fails it if the result lands more than 5% below the quote. The mint also needs a TAO/USD price no older than 300 blocks, about an hour.

Gamma’s valuation rule decides how much credit a burn buys. The protocol values the burned alpha in TAO, then converts that figure to dollars through an on-chain TAO/USD price feed. The TAO value equals alpha multiplied by the lower of two prices, the gamma price and the spot price, which the docs write as alpha × min(gamma price, spot price).

Every subnet keeps a gamma price. When a subnet registers, the price starts at the median alpha price across subnets. After that it moves asymmetrically. If spot falls, the gamma price falls to match at once. If spot rises, the gamma price climbs slowly toward it, closing a small slice of the gap each block, so the gap halves every 600 blocks, roughly two hours. However high spot jumps, the gamma price can at most double every 600 blocks.An example shows the effect. Say a user burns 100 alpha when spot sits at 0.05 TAO but the gamma price lags at 0.04. The mint uses 0.04, which gives 4 TAO of value, and at $400 per TAO that mints 1,600 gamma. Had the gamma price caught up, the same burn would mint 2,000, so the lag costs the burner 400 gamma. A short-lived pump buys no extra credit. The figures are illustrative, but the rule comes straight from the docs.The TAO/USD feed gets similar damping. A root-controlled oracle supplies the price, and the accepted price falls to a lower feed immediately but rises at most 66 parts per million per block, about 2% an hour. The docs admit the oracle is trusted: its accepted price can climb up to roughly 61% a day until root replaces or removes it.One more detail matters. The docs say alpha is valued at these prices, not at what selling it would return, so a burn that is large relative to the pool is worth more than a sale would be. A big burner gets credit for full value instead of a slipped sale price.Once minted, gamma holds its dollar value whether TAO or alpha prices rise or fall. Service providers still set their own prices.

To use a service, a person or an AI agent signs a request with a hotkey from their Bittensor wallet. The subnet owner, or another authorized account, deducts the required credits from that hotkey's gamma balance before delivering the service. Nothing transfers to anyone. The designated spender calls `spend-gamma` with up to 512 entries per call, each naming a hotkey, an amount and a 32-byte reference, and the spent gamma is destroyed on the spot.The reference doubles as a receipt. By convention it holds the service's own ID for the request being paid, returned with the response, so the customer can match each spend to a specific request. The chain repeats the reference in its events and reads it nowhere else, so an entry sent twice spends twice.Customers keep control throughout. The minting coldkey can set a daily spend cap that refills linearly over 7,200 blocks, about a day, and a cap of zero pauses the deposit. The coldkey can also change the spender, keep separate deposits for different apps and agents, and top up an existing deposit without switching hotkeys. Because the coldkey can pause or redirect at any moment, services spend ahead: they spend what they are about to serve, then serve what was spent. A spender can hand this right to a `GammaSpend` proxy, which can make no other call.Both minting and spending leave public records on-chain, so anyone can audit how much credit a subnet has created and how much customers have used.

The limits are strict. Gamma can't be transferred to another wallet, and it can't be converted back into alpha or TAO. It confers no claim on any party and can't be redeemed. Each subnet chooses whether, and at what prices, it accepts its own gamma.

The docs flag the sharpest risk directly: dissolving or pruning a subnet destroys all of its gamma, and holders receive nothing. A customer who prepaid a large deposit to a subnet that later shuts down loses it. Moving gamma between your own deposits is allowed, and a deposit opened under someone else's hotkey stays yours, since you can pull the gamma back at any time.A coldkey swap adds a few wrinkles. While one is announced, the coldkey's gamma calls are refused, though its spenders keep spending. After a subnet owner swaps coldkeys, deposits that name the old one keep it until the owner republishes its service.

The docs answer the economic question in one sentence: spent gamma pays its spender nothing. The value of the burned alpha accrues to the subnet's alpha holders.

That makes gamma a direct demand mechanism for alpha. Creating gamma always burns the subnet's alpha, which removes those tokens from circulation for good. When customers pay with TAO, the protocol first buys alpha from the subnet's pool, so TAO-funded purchases add buying pressure before the burn. Every dollar of AI usage ties a purchase of service credits to a burn of alpha.

A service operator earns through the alpha it holds and the emissions its subnet receives, not through a payment from customers. The structure rewards subnets that attract real usage, since usage shrinks their alpha supply.Two questions remain open. Customers get dollar-denominated credit, but the burn that funds it follows alpha prices, so heavy usage during a price spike may feel expensive. Holders also carry the dissolution risk, which will push careful buyers toward established subnets. Which services accept gamma, and at what price, will show whether this becomes a real payments layer or a niche tool. The mechanism is clear, and adoption is the unknown.

#5264. Ripple's RLUSD Overtakes PayPal's PYUSD

Ripple's US dollar-backed stablecoin RLUSD has set a new record by surpassing PayPal USD (PYUSD) in market capitalization to cement its position as a top stablecoin globally.

Recent data from CoinGecko shows that RLUSD's market cap has grown to around $2.71 billion, enabling it to surpass its competitor, PayPal's stablecoin, with a market cap of around $2.69 billion.

This milestone was achieved less than two years after Ripple's formal introduction of RLUSD in December 2024, underscoring its rapid growth in the crypto market.

A prominent XRP Ledger validator, Vet, also commented on this development to underscore the increasing significance of RLUSD in the stablecoin industry.

"RLUSD is now a Top 5 USD backed stablecoin. On its way to be in Top 3," Vet commented.

Vet noted Ripple's long-standing contribution to building the XRP Ledger. He added that the increasing adoption of RLUSD could potentially lead to faster adoption of the blockchain by traditional financial institutions.

Vet stressed the increasing relevance of RLUSD's rising payment volume and increased use of the stablecoin on the XRP Ledger.

He also noted that RLUSD has opened the door to numerous integrations with banks and crypto exchanges.

The XRP Ledger validator further noted that these integrations could motivate financial institutions to not only run infrastructure to support the XRPL but also integrate other tokenized assets on it.

This new record for RLUSD comes on the back of several key institutional partnerships and exchange integrations for RLUSD that Ripple has been announcing recently.

On Oct. 28, Ripple announced a partnership with Coinbase to provide RLUSD for retail and institutional users across Coinbase Exchange, Coinbase Prime and its retail trading app.

As part of the partnership, Coinbase also announced support for RLUSD across different blockchain networks such as the XRP Ledger, Ethereum and Base.

On the other hand, Ripple's partnership with banking giant BNY, which is the custodian of reserves for RLUSD, is also deepening.

Besides this, Ripple has also managed to secure support from Standard Chartered, which launched institutional custody services for RLUSD on the XRP Ledger back in October.

#5263. Why Is Crypto Crashing Today? Bitcoin Falls Below $73K as Zcash (ZEC) Leads Crypto Losses

Why is crypto crashing? A hot CPI report raised Fed hike bets. ZEC fell below $1,000, the worst of 20 large coins this week.

Why is crypto crashing on Wednesday, November 11? The sell-off that began with Tuesday’s hotter-than-expected U.S. inflation report has carried into today, and almost every major coin is lower.

Bitcoin (BTC) dropped below $73,000 on Tuesday, touching $72,727 on Binance, and now trades at about $73,800. Ether (ETH) briefly slipped to $2,006, while XRP and Solana (SOL) are down 2% to 3% in 24 hours. The Crypto Fear & Greed Index, a daily gauge of market mood from 0 to 100, has fallen to 29.

The report changed what traders expect from the Federal Reserve. Bond yields jumped, and bets on a larger December rate hike nearly tripled within two hours.

One coin is falling much harder than the rest. Zcash (ZEC) is a cryptocurrency launched in 2016 that lets users hide the sender, the receiver and the amount of a payment. It dropped below $1,000 on Wednesday for the first time since September 5. ZEC now trades at about $966, down 15.4% in 24 hours and 24.8% in a week.

ZEC has been one of this year’s best performers. It rose from about $526 on January 1 to a closing high of $1,653 on September 26. We checked the 20 largest coins on Binance, and ZEC fell the most over both the day and the week, even though it is still up 89% in 2026.

Trader 0x8742 opened a 10x long on 18,000 $ZEC ($17.63M) and is now down over $2.8M.

Liquidation price: $895.46.https://t.co/azzt3xvmay pic.twitter.com/wczndt7doC

— Lookonchain (@lookonchain) November 11, 2026

So why are the markets spooked, and why is ZEC taking the hardest hit?

Inflation came in hot. The consumer price index (CPI) rose 0.4% in October, above the 0.3% economists expected. Core prices, which leave out food and energy, rose 0.3% against a 0.2% forecast.

That reading crossed a line the Fed had drawn. Fed Governor Christopher Waller said in a speech hours before the report that core inflation of about 0.3% would make a half-point hike in December worth considering.

Traders took him at his word. On Polymarket, the odds of a hike of 0.5 percentage point or more in December went from 4.4% just before the report to 12.8% two hours later. They sit at 9.4% now, while a standard quarter-point hike is priced at 85.5%.

Higher rates hurt crypto in a simple way. They make cash and bonds pay more, so money flows out of riskier bets. On Tuesday, the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield rose from 4.86% to 4.98%.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best Low-Cap Crypto

ZEC had the most to give back. We compared the price changes of 20 large coins on Binance over the past week and since January 1.

When markets get nervous, traders tend to sell what has made them the most money. ZEC has fallen 41% from its September 26 closing high of $1,653.

Borrowed money made the drop faster. On Hyperliquid, ZEC fell from $1,199.20 to $965.79 in less than a day. Lookonchain counted 32 traders holding more than $1 million each in leveraged bets on a rising ZEC price. Of those, 27 are now losing money, with about $23.7 million in paper losses between them.

Sharp drops have not always lasted. Since January 2025, ZEC has fallen 12% or more in a single day 14 times on Binance. Seven days later, it was higher eight times, with a median gain of 6.5%.

EXPLORE: Fed Meeting Today: Traders Price a 95% Hold and a 79% December Hike. What Does It Mean for Crypto?

ZEC trades at about $966. It touched $961.07 on Wednesday, its lowest price since September 4.

On the daily chart, where each candle covers one day, ZEC has fallen below its 50-day exponential moving average (EMA), an average that gives recent prices more weight, at $1,200.68. It is still above its 200-day EMA at $872.23.

For Bitcoin, the line to watch is Tuesday’s low of $72,727. Below that, $68,902, the August 20 low, is the next support.

So, why is crypto crashing? A hot inflation report raised the odds of a bigger Fed hike, and ZEC’s leveraged bulls are paying the most for it. A daily close back above $1,050 would be the first sign the selling is easing.

#5262. Bitcoin to Witness First Back-to-Back Annual Losses as 2027 Could Spell More Trouble: Peter Schiff

Prominent Bitcoin critic Peter Schiff has pointed out that the premier cryptocurrency is on track to post back-to-back calendar-year losses for the first time in its history. If the situation persists and bulls are unable to stage a quick recovery, the digital currency could see a major price decline the following year as well.

Schiff noted that Bitcoin had never posted consecutive calendar-year declines in its roughly 18-year history. The digital asset posted a 6.34% price decrease in 2025, and it is already down 16.5% based on the latest spot price. He warned investors to be wary of this trend-defying move, which could result in major losses in 2027 as well.

While Schiff is known for criticizing digital currency only when it is on a downturn, the statistics he presented are accurate. Bitcoin closed 2025 lower by about 6.3% to 6.4%, ending near $87,500 after starting the year around $93,400–$93,500. It recorded a new all-time high (ATH) of $127.5k in October 2025, but failed to hold those gains by the end of December.

As of 2026, the cryptocurrency started the year around the $86k price level and is currently changing hands around $73k, representing a loss of more than 16%. It is highly likely that the digital currency won’t experience a price rebound in the last 6 weeks of the year, and it will make it two out of two for bearish years.

Historically, Bitcoin’s loss-reporting calendar years have been solo occurrences. In most instances when the premier digital currency witnesses a major contraction, like that in the years 2014 (roughly –56% to –58%), 2018 (around –73% to –74%), and 2022 (about –64%), it has followed it up with major gains in 2015, 2019, and 2023, respectively.

As a result, most years have been positive. If Bitcoin has had a hiccup, it has immediately followed it with a strong performance, which we are not seeing in 2026 or in the bearish end of 2025. However, 2025 was barely a downward trend, with a small 6.5% net price decrease. It can be considered a net price-neutral performance, which would make 2026 the year of a major price pullback and 2027 the year of a significant turnaround for the bulls.

Schiff has long argued that Bitcoin and other digital currencies have no intrinsic value and are not a store of value like Gold, which he promotes endlessly.

#5261. XRP, ETH, DOGE: Tim Draper Predicts Bitcoin to Absorb Altcoins

Billionaire and longtime Bitcoin (BTC) supporter Tim Draper predicts a future where Bitcoin absorbs the innovations of other altcoins.

Draper's statement has major implications for big cryptocurrencies like XRP, Ethereum (ETH) and Dogecoin (DOGE), which have built their own ecosystems and now compete in the wider cryptocurrency market.

In a recent post on X, Draper compared Bitcoin's rising dominance to Microsoft's path to becoming the dominant software company, as the company absorbed successful innovations from other businesses.

"Microsoft never invented the spreadsheet, word processor, or slide deck. They absorbed them," stated Draper.

The billionaire investor brought up pioneering software like Lotus 1-2-3 and WordPerfect, which eventually saw their dominance give way to Microsoft's Excel and Word.

Draper predicts that this could apply to the cryptocurrency industry, as Bitcoin could become the ultimate absorber of innovations from alternative blockchain networks.

"Altcoins are the Lotus 1-2-3s and WordPerfects of this time," wrote Draper.

Smaller cryptocurrencies are thus essentially incubators for technological innovations that could eventually become part of the bigger Bitcoin ecosystem, according to Draper.

"They show that it works, then the innovation that pulls the strongest gets ported to the Bitcoin platform," he added.

Draper also supported his statement by citing the rising market share of Bitcoin in the overall cryptocurrency market.

The billionaire investor recalled observing how Bitcoin dominance rose from about 40% to 50% and then even further to 61%.

"Bitcoin is that platform," said Draper, claiming that the biggest cryptocurrency could follow a path similar to Microsoft's.

This statement has implications for the future of big altcoins like Ethereum, XRP and Dogecoin.

Ethereum is the leading smart contract and dApp platform, while XRP is mainly known for its cross-border payments and the wider XRP Ledger ecosystem. Meanwhile, Dogecoin is one of the most iconic meme coins in the cryptocurrency market.

Still, the growing ecosystem around Bitcoin, which adds more scaling and programmability through solutions such as the Lightning Network and projects like Stacks, shows how Bitcoin is trying to expand beyond its basic use case as a cryptocurrency.

The bank’s call rests on three months of hot data. Consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, and core prices, which leave out food and energy because they swing the most, rose 0.3%. Both beat forecasts, the third upside surprise in a row in the Bureau of Labor Statistics report.

Bank of America now estimates that core PCE inflation, the Fed’s preferred measure, is running at 3.3% a year. The Fed’s target is 2%. The bank says price rises are spreading from goods to services, with electronics, airfares and hotels leading the increases.

Its base case is still a 25 bps hike in December. The change is in the risks: a 50 bps move is now possible, and the bank sees a growing chance of another hike in January instead of March.

The bank is not alone. Fed Governor Christopher Waller said in a speech on Tuesday morning that he leans toward a 25 bps hike in December. If core inflation came in around 0.3% again, he said, a 50 bps hike “should be considered.” It did.

Higher rates make cash and bonds pay more. That tends to pull money out of risky assets like BTC, and a faster pace of hikes pulls harder.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best New Crypto to Hodl

The size of the hike has mattered for BTC. We measured Bitcoin’s price on Binance from the 2 p.m. ET announcement of each Fed rate hike since 2022 to one week later. That covers 12 hikes: six of 50 bps or more and six of 25 bps.

After the six big hikes, BTC was lower a week later five times. The median move was a 6% drop. The worst came after the 50 bps hike in May 2022, when BTC fell 23% in a week.

After the six 25 bps hikes, the picture was milder. BTC was lower a week later four times, but the median move was a drop of just 0.6%.

The record comes with a caveat. All six big hikes happened in 2022, a bear market that also saw the collapses of Terra in May and FTX in November. Those crashes made the falls after the May and November hikes worse.

The most recent hike was a 25 bps move on September 16. BTC rose 11.3% in the week after it, as the uncertainty that had built up before the meeting cleared. That makes the size of December’s hike, more than the hike itself, the Bitcoin news to watch.

DISCOVER: Bitcoin CPI Reaction: 10 of 13 Cool Inflation Reports Triggered an Hourly Gain – Can Inflation Data Reverse the Downtrend?

BTC trades at $73,888, down 0.6% in 24 hours and 5.8% over the past week. It sits below both of its exponential moving averages (EMAs), averages that give recent prices more weight, on the daily chart. The 50-day EMA stands at $78,897 and the 200-day EMA at $76,449.

For Bitcoin news, the next test is the Fed’s own message. Traders already expect a 25 bps hike. If more officials join Waller and Bank of America in backing 50 bps, BTC may have to defend $72,727 before the December 9 decision.

#5254. XRP Ledger Announces Major Fix to Come December 3

The XRP Ledger (XRPL) will be delivering a major update on Dec. 3, which will address the occasional sluggishness the blockchain network has been experiencing in recent weeks.

As stated in a recent XRP Ledger Operations announcement, the network will be rolling out its new version 3.5.0, which will exclusively include technical improvements and bug fixes, such as a lasting fix for the relatively slow ledger closing times.

"XRPL version 3.5.0 will be on Dec 3. Just improvements/fixes, including a long-lasting fix for the occasional slow ledger close times," XRP Ledger Operations said.

"Interim fixes already helped improve close times, and we are watching the network very closely," it added.

This is a critical advancement in improving the reliability of the XRP Ledger, a network widely used to process cryptocurrency payments, tokenization, and stablecoin transactions.

The latest improvement to the XRPL comes after the blockchain network suffered technical issues in October, when some ledgers were closing much slower than usual.

The XRP Ledger usually closes new ledgers once every three to five seconds. This ensures that transaction confirmations happen fairly quickly.

However, intermittent sluggishness was seen on the network, as XRP Ledger Operations admitted on Oct. 21. The team later confirmed that its developers were already working on the issue.

Afterward, XRP Ledger Operations started sharing a recommended configuration update for xrpld software with network operators such as validators and other infrastructure providers.

The temporary fixes were helpful. On Oct. 22, XRP Ledger Operations shared that the occasional slower ledger closures were no longer happening, thanks to the new recommended configuration.

That said, the developers remain hard at work to deliver a software fix that will correct the issue once and for all, a long-term solution that would not rely solely on temporary changes.

That is why the December release is expected to finally bring that permanent fix.

In a recent post on X, he stressed that a great amount of work has been put into network monitoring, information security and engineering.

Vet said that their engineers are always on call to address any possible incidents.

#5253. Solana Lands Major Wall Street Boost as DTCC Targets 2027 Launch of Tokenized Assets: What It Means for SOL

Wall Street is taking another major step toward blockchain adoption, and Solana (SOL) is emerging as one of the networks positioned to benefit. The Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation (DTCC), the financial infrastructure giant that clears and settles much of the U.S. securities market, plans to bring its tokenization services to Solana in 2027.

The move could open the door to tokenized stocks, exchange-traded funds (ETFs), and U.S. Treasuries on the blockchain, marking a significant institutional milestone for Solana. But beyond the headline announcement, the obvious question is what this development could mean for the price of SOL and its long-term investment appeal.

DTCC announced Thursday that it plans to extend its tokenization services to Solana in the second half of 2027. The initiative will connect its DTCC Tokenization Service to the Layer 1 blockchain, enabling eligible securities held by its Depository Trust Company subsidiary to be represented as digital tokens.

BREAKING: @The_DTCC to tokenize custodied assets on Solana. announced plans to connect the DTCC Tokenization Service to Solana, enabling the tokenization of eligible DTC-custodied assets on the network.The integration is planned for the second half of 2027, further advancing… pic.twitter.com/gXszWFgUOX

“DTC-tokenized assets made available on Solana – and all blockchain networks integrated with the service – will retain the same investor protections, ownership rights and regulatory safeguards that apply to traditionally held securities,” Brian Steele, president of DTCC Clearing & Securities Services, said in the announcement.

DTCC’s Tokenization Service went live on October 28, initially operating on the Canton Network and the corporation’s own private blockchain, which is built on the Besu framework. The platform allows eligible participants to convert traditional securities into tokenized assets and redeem them back into their original form, with the digital tokens delivered directly to wallets of their choice. At launch, DTCC also outlined plans to expand its tokenization service to additional blockchain networks in 2027, with Stellar and Circle’s Arc among the platforms also slated for integration.

Solana has been stepping up efforts to attract traditional financial institutions, positioning itself as a blockchain capable of supporting large-scale financial activity. Nick Ducoff, head of institutional growth at the Solana Foundation, recently highlighted this appeal, stating that institutions choose Solana because it already “runs real financial activity at scale.” He added that firms are already issuing assets, settling transactions, and deploying capital on the network, according to a post shared by Solana’s official X account.

The potential opportunity becomes clearer when considering DTCC’s position in the U.S. financial system. Through its Depository Trust Company (DTC) subsidiary, the financial infrastructure giant holds approximately $114 trillion in securities on behalf of banks and brokerage firms. Its newly launched tokenization service initially covered 34 eligible securities representing an estimated $30 trillion in potential tokenized assets. However, this figure reflects the value of securities eligible for tokenization, not assets already issued or circulating on blockchain networks.

Bringing even a fraction of this enormous securities market onto Solana could translate into substantial institutional activity and settlement volumes over time. This could create additional opportunities for SOL demand if the token is required for relevant network transactions. Nevertheless, the integration is not expected until the second half of 2027, making the development a potential long-term growth driver rather than an immediate price catalyst. Its ultimate impact will depend on institutional adoption, actual transaction volumes, and whether increased network activity translates into meaningful demand for SOL.
