#5206. Why Social Security Cuts Could Cost $500 a Month

Home » Regulations » Why Social Security Cuts Could Cost $500 a Month

A $10.8 trillion payroll tax gap is accelerating Social Security’s 2032 shortfall—and reshaping retirement and investment strategies.

For years, the impending Social Security funding crunch has been framed as a simple demographic math problem: Baby Boomers are retiring faster than younger workers can replace them.

While an aging population plays a role, a new economic analysis reveals a far bigger, largely overlooked culprit—a structural shift in how U.S. income is earned and taxed that has quietly starved the program of $10.8 trillion and shaved a quarter-century off its solvency timeline.

According to a November 2026 study from the AARP Public Policy Institute, the program’s trust funds could have paid 100% of scheduled benefits until 2059 if the share of the U.S. economy subject to payroll taxes had simply held steady at 1983 levels.

Instead, the retirement fund is projected to deplete its reserves in late 2032, putting millions of Americans on track for automatic Social Security cuts exceeding $500 a month.

Social Security relies on payroll taxes for roughly 91% of its annual funding, according to the 2026 Social Security Trustees Report. However, a shrinking slice of U.S. economic output comes from traditional wages covered by that tax.

AARP’s analysis found that wages subject to Social Security payroll taxes accounted for 41% of U.S. gross domestic product (GDP) in 1983. By 2025, that share had fallen to 34%. That 7% represents an estimated $10.8 trillion in lost tax revenue and interest between 1984 and 2034.

The report attributes this erosion to several modern economic shifts:

Under current projections from the Social Security Administration, the Old-Age and Survivors Insurance (OASI) trust fund, which pays retirement and survivor benefits, will run out of reserves in the fourth quarter of 2032.

If Congress were to merge it with the separate Disability Insurance trust fund, combined reserves would last until 2034.

Depletion does not mean Social Security payments will stop entirely, because active workers will continue paying payroll taxes into the system. However, without legislative action, incoming tax revenue will only cover 78% of scheduled retirement benefits in 2032 (or 83% on a combined basis in 2034).

That translates to an automatic 22% across-the-board cut in 2032—reducing the average retiree’s monthly check by more than $500 in over half of U.S. states.

With less than six years before the 2032 deadline, lawmakers face a narrow window to either broaden how the program captures revenue from a shifting economy or let an automatic benefit reduction take effect by default.

A 22% reduction in Social Security payouts would directly compress disposable income for tens of millions of U.S. households, reshaping consumer spending, personal savings rates, and long-term fiscal deficit projections.

First, concerns about the long-term future of Social Security could lead some younger Americans to take more responsibility for their own retirement savings. For some investors, that may mean looking beyond traditional retirement accounts to alternative assets, including Bitcoin and crypto ETFs.

Second, proposals to strengthen Social Security by taxing a broader range of income could have implications for financial markets. If lawmakers eventually target investment income or adjust capital gains taxes, the changes could affect investor behavior and market liquidity across both traditional and digital asset markets.

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

TL;DR: Sygnum has announced an ETH-denominated fund targeting 8–10% annual returns after fees. The target includes staking income, and investors remain exposed to ETH's market price.

Sygnum is pitching a different measure of investment performance: how much Ether an investor owns at the end of the year. In its November 12 announcement, the bank introduced the ETH Alpha Fund, which opened to investors on November 2 and is aimed at professional and qualified investors in approved markets.

The fund's product page makes two distinctions explicit. Its 8–10% objective is the total portfolio target, including staking. It is also denominated in ETH, so the value of an investment in dollars or another currency continues to move with Ether's price.

That changes how the headline number should be read. As a hypothetical illustration, an investor starting with 100 ETH and achieving an 8% token return would finish with 108 ETH. If the dollar price of Ether fell 20% over the same period, the position's dollar value would still be 13.6% lower.

That example describes arithmetic, not a forecast for the fund. It shows why increasing a token balance and preserving purchasing power are different objectives. The meaning of a successful year depends on which currency the investor uses to measure it.

Sygnum says the portfolio combines native staking with options premiums, arbitrage and derivatives carry or funding strategies. The trading component aims to earn returns without relying on a directional call on ETH.

Ethereum's staking documentation explains the underlying distinction. Validators receive rewards for their role in maintaining the network. They can also lose ETH through inactivity penalties or slashing, while using a service provider adds another counterparty to the arrangement.

Trading income has a separate economic source. An options premium compensates the seller for accepting an obligation; an arbitrage strategy depends on a pricing difference that can be captured after costs. Neither is simply an extra protocol reward.

Combining these activities may diversify the sources of income. It also makes the resulting product more complex to evaluate than a straightforward staking position.

The launch announcement says trading uses Sygnum Protect, keeping collateral off exchanges at the bank. The product page lists a minimum subscription of $100,000 or its ETH equivalent, monthly subscriptions and monthly redemptions, with advance notice requirements. It also lists an investor-level gate of up to 10%, although the page does not explain its mechanics.

Those terms matter for an institution that must meet cash demands on a different timetable. A quoted asset value does not necessarily mean that capital can be withdrawn immediately. A treasury evaluating such a structure has to match its investment horizon with the fund's dealing arrangements.

Custody deserves the same attention. NewsBTC's coverage of Sygnum's MultiSYG lending arrangement illustrates how the control of collateral can be designed separately from the financial exposure attached to it.

This launch sits within the broader expansion of institutional ETH products, alongside developments such as Amundi's Ethereum-based fund share class. The products serve different purposes, even though both use Ethereum-related infrastructure.

For the new fund, the useful evidence will be realised returns, the consistency of those returns and how its strategies behave when market conditions change. Comparisons also need the same accounting basis: net with net, ETH with ETH and equivalent observation periods.

An annual target gives investors an objective to assess. A live track record will show how closely the fund can follow it.

#5202. Bitcoin Drops Below $68K as Buyers Quietly Vanish

Home » Bitcoin (BTC) » Bitcoin Drops Below $68K as Buyers Quietly Vanish

On-chain metrics show a massive 362,000 BTC demand gap opening up across major markets.

Bitcoin crashed below the key $70,000 support level on Friday, hitting a three-month low of $67,650 as a sudden leadership crisis at Nvidia, new MSCI index rules, and hot U.S. inflation rattled global markets.

Bitcoin fell 8.6% in 24 hours to $67,650 on early Friday, its lowest mark since August 19, extending a 10.2% weekly decline.

While yesterday’s pullback below $73,000 was driven largely by macroeconomic jitters, Friday’s breakdown reflects a rare convergence of tech-sector turmoil, institutional index risks, and evaporating spot liquidity.

Adding structural pressure to crypto equities, index provider MSCI’s November Index Review has placed Bitcoin treasury companies, including Michael Saylor’s Strategy (MSTR) and Tokyo-listed Metaplanet, at risk of losing their place in major stock market indexes.

Under MSCI’s updated eligibility rules companies that hold too much of their assets in investments rather than running an operating business could lose their eligibility for indexes such as the MSCI USA and MSCI World.

When a company is dropped from a major index, funds that track it often have to sell their shares, which can drive down demand and put pressure on the stock price.

Strategy’s shares dropped 6.49% in extended trading on Thursday. The company has previously warned that eventual removal from MSCI indexes could force passive funds to sell around $2.8 billion worth of its shares.

For Bitcoin, the bigger concern is that Strategy could slow its Bitcoin purchases if it becomes harder or more expensive to raise money. That would remove a major source of buying demand just as U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs have recorded five consecutive days of outflows totaling $1.43 billion, according to SoSoValue.

Market sentiment weakened further on November 12 after Nvidia announced that CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang was stepping down with immediate effect. CFO Colette Kress was named interim CEO.

Huang’s abrupt departure follows an internal board investigation and media reports detailing alleged extramarital affairs, including one with a alleged Chinese spy as well as relationships with Nvidia employees.

Nvidia shares fell as much as 4% on Thursday, extending a month-long decline that has wiped out 27.28% of the stock’s value. The Nvidia news added to pressure on risk assets, alongside declines in the Nasdaq Composite (-0.39%) and S&P 500 (-0.35%).

Rising inflation is adding pressure to both stock and crypto markets. The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, above the 0.3% forecast. Core inflation, which excludes food and energy, also came in higher than expected at 0.3%, against a forecast of 0.2%.

The higher-than-expected figures have reduced hopes of near-term interest rate cuts and raised expectations of a rate hike.

According to CME Group’s FedWatch tool, markets are now pricing in an 88.5% chance of a 0.25-percentage-point rate increase in December. Higher interest rates could put further pressure on Bitcoin by making safer investments, such as U.S. Treasury bonds, more attractive

Blockchain data suggests Bitcoin lacked enough buying demand to defend the $70,000 level.

According to a CryptoQuant report, demand across spot and perpetual futures markets fell by 362,000 BTC over 30 days, with spot demand declining by 280,000 BTC and futures demand by 82,000 BTC.

Meanwhile, Bitcoin miner transfers to exchanges surged to 2,077 BTC on November 10, roughly 16 times the 30-day daily average of 127 BTC. About 97% of the transfers came from Antpool.

At the same time, stablecoin supply contracted by $14.2 billion over 30 days, pointing to declining liquidity across the crypto market.

According to CryptoQuant analysts, the broader picture remains cautious. Leverage is being unwound, but fresh spot buying has yet to return convincingly. Until demand strengthens, ETF flows turn positive and market liquidity stabilizes, Bitcoin’s recovery is likely to remain fragile, with further downside risks still in play.

#5201. Bitcoin volatility falls to 45% – Here’s what it does NOT mean for BTC

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Crypto evaluation, especially for Bitcoin [BTC], tends to be shifting from highly volatile to a mature asset. Bitcoin volatility has fallen to 45% over its 18 years of existence, within the range of common large-cap U.S. stocks.

For instance, JPMorgan and Amazon are at 80% and 90%, respectively, meaning they are a bit more volatile than BTC. Oracle, Coinbase, Micron, and Sandisk are more stable, with their volatilities well below 20%.

This current reading of Bitcoin volatility reflects an asset that has matured with greater institutional participation. However, this does not mean that BTC is now a low-risk asset.

Therefore, the asset deserves another risk framework different from how it was viewed in the past 10 years. During its initial stages, the volatility was exceeding 100% against a capitalization of single-digit billions.

Interestingly, during periods of strong positive momentum, Bitcoin’s gains were achieved faster than the downside deviation as per the Sortino ratio. Still, that does not negate sudden and more aggressive nosedives.

Therefore, maturity has been driven by clearer regulations, more secure investment vehicles like ETFs, and institutional involvement. BlackRock, Grayscale, Strategy, and Morgan Stanley are a few of the deeply involved institutions in BTC adoption.

The maturity of Bitcoin has created opportunities for a more diversified crypto portfolio. Other crypto sectors are becoming less tied to Bitcoin’s price performance, an edge ahead of traditional assets.

Most traditional assets are related to one another.

For instance, the annualized volatility of Smart Contracts Platforms is at 58%, with BTC contributing 38% while sector-specific drive was 20%.

However, Artificial Intelligence (AI) was at 85%, probably because it was somehow new in the financial markets. For this, Bitcoin-driven volatility was 35%, while sector-specific was 50%.

Events like the resignation of the CEO of Nvidia, Jensen Huang, after having an affair with a Chinese spy, have greatly impacted the AI market sector.

Other sectors in crypto, like financials, are at 59%, with 30% being Bitcoin-driven. This phenomenon is quite evident with seasonality in the crypto market.

But Bitcoin seasons are characterized by selective altcoin performance. On the other hand, altcoin seasons have BTC being performed by more than 75 alts in the top 100 by capitalization. Currently, only 45 altcoins have performed better than Bitcoin in the past 90 days.

All in all, crypto maturity is not only on Bitcoin but also in the whole sector. Therefore, a crypto risk framework should be done across more than one dimension to reflect its evolution.

#5200. Chainstack Traces Customer Data Breach to Exposed Admin Tools

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: Chainstack’s expanded incident report focuses on access-control failures. Its recovery guidance makes completed credential rotation a priority.

Chainstack has added technical detail to the security incident it first disclosed on November 3. Its updated report, with a technical section dated November 10, describes an October intrusion built around configuration and access-control failures. The company says it found no evidence that a software vulnerability was exploited.

According to Chainstack, the attacker entered through a development Grafana instance with unchanged default administrator credentials. An unauthenticated tool server with broad Kubernetes permissions then formed part of the access path. Machine credentials also connected the development and production environments.

The operational lesson is about the reach of an account after the first login. A low-profile testing service can become consequential if it can contact sensitive systems or holds privileges that extend beyond its immediate job.

NewsBTC's coverage of the NEAR AI infrastructure incident explored a related boundary between an application and the services supporting it. The mechanisms differ, but both make the surrounding infrastructure relevant to a crypto platform's security.

The report identifies account names, organisation details, email addresses and password hashes as potentially exposed. It treats node credentials as exposed despite finding no evidence they were read, and asks customers to change passwords, rotate node credentials and regenerate platform API keys where used.

A password hash and a working access token create different problems. Hashes are representations of passwords, while an active token may directly authorise requests. Replacing a login password therefore cannot be assumed to invalidate every other credential associated with an application.

This is why incident guidance needs to identify the affected credential types clearly. A single instruction to change a password can leave developers uncertain about application endpoints, automated jobs and service integrations.

Chainstack's node-management documentation describes a staged rotation process. New credentials are generated while the existing ones remain active. Applications can then move to the replacements before the old credentials are deactivated.

The documentation says both sets continue working until that final step, with no automatic time limit. Completing the rotation permanently rejects requests using the previous credentials. It also says a node rotation does not change a multichain authentication token.

For an operator, the overlap reduces the risk of interrupting a working service while updating applications. The corresponding responsibility is to finish the migration. Generating a replacement alone leaves the previous means of access available.

A useful completion record would therefore track which applications have moved and when the old credentials were disabled. That is a practical control a team can verify after the initial emergency.

Grafana's security guidance warns that services on its local network may be reachable through its data-source proxy. It describes controls such as limiting permitted destinations and using firewall rules to restrict access to sensitive internal services.

Those precautions address what a tool can reach, as well as who can log into it. Authentication and network boundaries perform different jobs; permission limits provide another layer if either boundary fails.

NewsBTC's report on Chainalysis restoring screening services shows why operational recovery and data-exposure analysis can follow different timelines.

Chainstack's expanded account gives customers more detail to assess. The remaining test is whether access changes are completed and whether the revised controls can prevent one compromised service from reaching far beyond its intended role.

Trezor confirmed on the 12th of November that three Safe 5 hardware wallets sold by CryptoBilis contained malicious implants. Fortunately, no customer had reported losing funds.

Still, Trezor urged affected buyers to move their crypto after releasing a firmware fix.

Customers bought those 3 devices between the 20th of August and the 23rd of September through CryptoBilis directly or its Tokopedia and Shopee stores. Trezor examined one device in its lab and identified two more from customer photos.

48 buyers had contacted the company, and at press time, checks were ongoing. Trezor reported that there were no confirmed cases involving other models or resellers.

Apparently, the implants could take recovery phrases and passphrases that appeared on the wallet screen.

On X, a user asked how a software update could stop a physical implant from recording the display. Trezor explained that firmware could “listen to the communication between the MCU and the display,” and the firm has now changed the order of commands needed for the trigger.

Regardless, Trezor still urged buyers to use a fresh recovery phrase because “the update can’t protect a wallet backup that was captured before it.” This advice applied to customers who bought a Trezor from CryptoBilis from March 2026 onward.

The hardware wallet company also urged those using its devices to move funds to a new wallet with a fresh recovery phrase. It told buyers with unused devices to leave them unconfigured. Eligible buyers could contact Trezor Support for a replacement or a refund where shipping limited their options.

Trezor dropped CryptoBilis on the 9th of October after reports of tampered Ledger devices sold through them. A customer also flagged a suspected Safe 5 implant on the 28th of October.

Trezor issued a warning two days later, saying that it cut its reseller network by about 80% and tightened rules on sourcing, storage, and access.

This brought the debate back to what self-custody protects, and as Ledger CEO Pascal Gauthier said,

Everybody will be hacked at some point. Perfect security doesn’t exist.

#5197. Solo Brings Human Verification to Venmo Co-Founder’s JellyJelly App as AI Agents Beat CAPTCHA

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Solo’s SDK confirms that each JellyJelly account belongs to a real, unique person, after a Solo AI agent passed CAPTCHA on 50+ Discord servers.

Magdon-Ismail is co-founder and CEO of JellyJelly and an advisor to Solo. He co-developed the SDK behind the integration, shaping both its architecture and the way new users are onboarded.

The move comes as AI agents learn to pass the tests meant to keep them out. In an experiment run by Solo, an AI agent named Gary joined more than 50 Discord servers overnight and sent over 500 messages. No one identified it as an AI agent.

Gary had two instructions: pass every CAPTCHA challenge and accept the terms of service. It completed both through ordinary browsing and clicking, without any custom exploits.

Solo reads the result as a weakness in CAPTCHA. The challenges test whether a visitor can solve a puzzle, and capable AI agents can solve the same puzzles. Harder tests add friction for legitimate users, but they do little to show that a human is behind an account.

“CAPTCHA was built around the idea that humans could do things bots couldn’t. That’s becoming a harder assumption to make when AI agents can browse, click and solve the same challenges as people,” said Edison Siu, co-founder and CEO of Solo. “Our approach is to verify the human directly. Platforms need to know they’re dealing with a real person. Users shouldn’t have to struggle through more puzzles or upload identity documents to prove it.”

JellyJelly lets users share short videos and send cryptocurrency payments to one another. The rise of AI-generated video and automated accounts has made it harder for social platforms to know who is behind each account. Solo’s SDK brings human verification into that setting. It helps the platform tell genuine users from automated accounts, and it stops one person from registering several verified identities.

The process starts with a facial scan from a standard smartphone camera. Solo converts the scan into a biometric representation and encrypts it on the device using fully homomorphic encryption (FHE). This type of encryption lets a system work on data without ever decrypting it. Solo uses it to compare the encrypted representation against existing records, so the matching step never exposes the underlying data.

Users do not need special hardware or a government-issued ID. Raw facial images are not stored. Apps that use the SDK receive a verification result, not access to anyone’s biometric information.

The same SDK can be added to gaming platforms, payment services and other applications that need to block duplicate accounts or separate real users from automated activity.

Solo is backed by Draper Associates, the venture firm founded by Tim Draper. Draper Associates led a $1 million round in the company in March 2025. Solo was also selected for cohort 5 of the Solana Incubator.

Solo’s human verification technology is already live. The company is now working on tools that would let verified users authorize their own AI agents, so merchants and online platforms can confirm that a real, unique person stands behind each one. Solo also plans to enable AI agents and AI companies to pay verified people for work that only humans can do.

Magdon-Ismail, who co-founded Venmo and helped develop its peer-to-peer payment system, is advising Solo on how people and their AI agents will pay and get paid.

“Venmo made it easy to pay a friend,” said Magdon-Ismail. “The next step is your AI agent paying on your behalf. The business receiving that payment needs to know a real person authorized it. I’m working with Solo to make that process simple for everyone involved.”

Solo develops proof-of-humanity technology that lets online platforms check that a user is a real, unique person, without asking who that person is. Its smartphone-based system uses fully homomorphic encryption to compare encrypted biometric data, and partners receive a verification result instead of raw biometric data. Solo provides an SDK for web and mobile applications. The company is backed by Draper Associates and was selected for the Solana Incubator cohort 5. Its first product, SoloMission, lets AI agents collect feedback from verified humans.

The filing shows that Rakuten held 6,690 shares of the Bitwise XRP ETF worth $111,255. At press time, the price of XRP stands at $1.03, and the shares of the Bitwise fund trade at $11.51, according to SoSoValue, so the XRP ETF stake of Rakuten is now worth about $77,000.

The largest position of Rakuten is in BlackRock's spot Bitcoin fund, the iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF, and Rakuten held $5,893,593 worth of its shares at the end of the third quarter. Besides, Rakuten owns $263,632 of the iShares Ethereum Trust ETF and $150,728 of the Bitwise Solana Staking ETF.

U.S. rules require any institutional manager holding more than $100 million in U.S. exchange-listed securities to disclose its portfolio every quarter, no matter where it's based. Rakuten Group holds about $1.4 billion in U.S. equities, and most of that amount is in shares of satellite operator AST SpaceMobile. In this context, the crypto ETF positions account for less than 0.5% of the U.S. portfolio of Rakuten.

Rakuten is one of the largest tech companies in Japan. The market capitalization of Rakuten stands at about ¥1.4 trillion ($9 billion), and the annual revenue of the company is more than ¥2.5 trillion ($16 billion).

The Rakuten ecosystem spans more than 70 services, from the Rakuten Ichiba marketplace and carrier Rakuten Mobile to banks and brokerages. According to Rakuten, these services have more than 100 million users in Japan and more than 2.1 billion users worldwide.

The latest filing comes amid outflows from spot XRP ETFs. According to SoSoValue, the funds lost $10.42 million on Nov. 9 and another $7.62 million on Nov. 10, and there were no flows on Nov. 11 and Nov. 12. On Oct. 28, the total net assets of the funds stood at $1.51 billion.

Still, the cumulative net inflow of spot XRP ETFs stands at $1.79 billion, and the total net assets of the funds are $1.16 billion, or 1.77% of the market cap of XRP. Finally, the Bitwise XRP ETF is the largest of the five spot XRP funds, and its net assets stand at $420.29 million, according to SoSoValue.

#5195. NYSE Taps Avalanche to Power Tokenized Stock Trading as Wall Street Embraces Blockchain Infrastructure

Home » Exchanges » NYSE Taps Avalanche to Power Tokenized Stock Trading as Wall Street Embraces Blockchain Infrastructure

NYSE has selected Avalanche technology to support settlement for its planned tokenized securities platform, bringing round-the-clock stock trading and faster settlement closer to reality, pending regulatory approval.

The New York Stock Exchange is mixing together blockchain technology and traditional finance. It selected Avalanche to power the settlement infrastructure of its upcoming tokenized securities platform. The decision is part of a growing effort to bring crypto trading and its benefits to traditional finance.

Announced on November 9, 2026, the partnership will see Avalanche provide the core ledger technology for the clearing firm supporting the NYSE-affiliated digital trading venue. One of the goals is to enable round-the-clock trading, as well as clearing and settlement of tokenized securities, all of which still require regulatory changes.

NYSE has organized a yearlong test, and afterwards Avalanche emerged as a favorite provider and one that could meet its needs and provide a seamless inclusion of blockchain traders into the fold of the stock exchange account holders.

The platform is designed to support equities issued across multiple blockchain networks, meaning Avalanche will not necessarily host every tokenized stock traded through the venue. The technology will therefore mostly be used to record and settle transactions.

NYSE Head of Digital Issuance Dennis Lee said that the focus was on speed, reliability, and predictable costs. Ava Labs CEO Emin Gün Sirer also highlighted the importance of dedicated infrastructure.

The crypto infrastructure industry is huge, and there’s a growing list of cryptocurrency exchanges, including those reviewed by CryptoManiaks, to choose from. Platforms made for transfers and smart contracts automating payments have also grown and now include thousands of providers. NYSE chose Avalanche due to some of its unique characteristics.

Avalanche’s architecture allows businesses to create dedicated blockchain networks with rules tailored to their operational and regulatory requirements. It creates a flexibility that traditional financial institutions are looking for.

Stock exchanges handle countless transactions, and stability is the most important feature they are looking for. Another important feature is atomic settlement. It allows the transfer of securities and corresponding payment to occur as part of the same transaction. Therefore, there’s no chance one side of a trade is completed while the other remains outstanding.

NYSE also plans to operate a custom blockchain built using Avalanche technology rather than relying directly on Avalanche’s public network.

The decision reflects a broader effort to tokenize traditional markets and get the best of both worlds. That way, crypto companies won’t dominate the space, but can combine their features with those of the stock market.

Nasdaq is among the NYSE’s most prominent competitors. It, too, has developed tokenized stock infrastructure and is pursuing partnerships that could help distribute blockchain-based securities. This is done in cooperation with Kraken and in a way that NYSE is responding to the demands of a competitive market.

The Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation (DTCC), a central institution in US securities settlements, also has plans to introduce tokenization. It plans to use blockchain to support securities custody and transfers.

NYSE has also expanded its list of partners. It now includes Broadridge Financial Solutions, Computershare, Equiniti, and Superstate. These developments show that financial institutions are fighting to establish the underlying infrastructure that will determine how digital securities are traded, transferred, and settled.

What Tokenized Stocks Could Mean for Investors

Tokenized stocks could change how investors are accessing traditional financial markets. The possibility of trading outside of business hours is the first thing investors have been looking for, alongside faster settlements. The NYSE’s broader platform plans include stablecoin-based funding, fractional share trading, and immediate settlement.

Ownership will also change. The NYSE has indicated that its platform will support tokenized shares that are fungible with traditionally issued securities, as well as securities originally issued in digital form. Shareholders will continue to have the same rights as traditional owners, meaning they’ll receive dividends and take part in corporate governance.

All of these benefits aren’t regulated, and before investors can take advantage of them, traditional regulatory bodies need to act and establish rules and guidelines for the new features.

Despite the institutional interest, the NYSE’s Avalanche-powered project still faces several challenges before it can become a functioning alternative to conventional securities infrastructure. The platform needs to demonstrate that it can maintain the safeguards expected of a major US stock exchange.

There’s also a distinction between Avalanche’s institutional adoption and the potential benefits for its native AVAX token. It’s not clear if the cooperation with NYSE will generate demand for AVAX. The project will depend on its ability to attract issuers, brokers, and investors while delivering reliable settlement.

After the largest hack in the history of crypto, Binance has announced that it has fully recovered all $6.3 billion in digital assets stolen during the cyberattack.

For those unaware, Binance initially recovered most of the stolen assets within days using company profits and emergency reserves, while the remaining 10% required additional time.

Well, the hack was so widespread that the operation involved more than 20,000 wallets and at least 65,000 transactions within a week, according to blockchain analytics firm Elliptic.

Of that, around $430,000 was also reportedly laundered through memecoins. Chainalysis also identified Chinese money-laundering networks as part of the cash conversion process.

But now Binance has made a complete comeback, and remarking on this 100% recovery, the exchange took to X and noted,

Once the zero-knowledge proof is generated, users can independently verify that their assets are backed at a minimum of 1:1.

To our users and community: thank you for your patience and understanding.

This coincided with Binance publishing an updated Proof of Reserves snapshot dated 12th November. According to reports, user BTC holdings rose 0.35% to 687,900 BTC, while ETH reserves increased 1.04% to 3.48 million ETH.

Meanwhile, BNB holdings also climbed 1.03% to 42.95 million tokens. However, USDT reserves declined 3.68% to 24.3 billion tokens.

However, the U.S. federal authorities and private-sector partners have frozen more than $2.7 billion in cryptocurrency stolen during the Binance cyberattack.

At the same time, the U.S. Department of Justice also secured court authorization to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion in stolen assets as efforts to trace the remaining funds continue.

This further coincided with the U.S. Department of Justice’s announcement of coordinated actions against North Korean cybercriminal operations responsible for cryptocurrency thefts worth billions of dollars.

In fact, one major operation, called FaceStealer, has reportedly stolen more than $400 million in cryptocurrency over the past 18 months.

Additionally, the FBI also seized cloud infrastructure used in the campaign and more than 900 webcam videos of victims.

#5193. Hyperscalers List GPUs at Nearly 2× the GPU-Cloud Price, Fluence Research Finds

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

The AI Compute Race report prices GPU compute outside the biggest buyers: a three-year commitment cuts the median price by 48%, while 17 of 22 tracked GPU models rose in price over the past year

DALLAS, Texas – November 13, 2026 – Fluence has published The AI Compute Race, a report that prices GPU cloud compute for every company that is not a frontier lab or a hyperscaler. It was produced with research partners NEAR AI, io.net, Boundless, Phala, Gensyn, Fortytwo, Theta, Compute Labs and GAIB. Its central finding: where a company buys a GPU-hour sets the price. Across H100, H200 and B200 models, hyperscalers list GPUs at 1.98 times the GPU-cloud median, from 1.4 times on the B200 to 2.8 times on the H100. The same H200 lists from $4.08 to $10.60 an hour.

Commitment length matters almost as much as provider choice. Against each provider’s own on-demand rate, a one-year reservation cuts the median price by 21% and a three-year term by 48%. Spot capacity lists at 53% of on-demand, for workloads that can be interrupted.

Buyers who expect GPU prices to fall may need to recheck their budgets. Seventeen of the 22 GPU models tracked by GetDeploying cost more than a year earlier, and the median H100 rents for 13% to 30% more, depending on the window measured.

The report also traces why prices are rapidly rising:

“Open-weight models are close behind the best closed ones, and companies are switching to them. Any company with GPUs can now serve a near-frontier model on hardware it controls. The GPUs are the hard part,” said Evgeny Ponomarev, Co-founder of Fluence.

The report closes with four ways to pay less for the same compute: compare the same chip across provider types, commit when the workload is steady, match the GPU generation to the model, and look beyond the hyperscalers, since much of the newest neocloud capacity is contracted to labs years ahead.

The full report is available at fluence.ai/compute-race-2026.

Fluence Cloud is a GPU cloud provider with capacity from independent data centers (fluence.ai). Founded in 2017 by Dmitry Kurinskiy, Evgeny Ponomarev and Tom Trowbridge, the company has raised $14 million from investors including 1KX, Multicoin, Distributed Global, Blockchange, Tiger Global and Protocol Labs.

Stellar (XLM), the blockchain co-founded by Jed McCaleb, has become the leader in daily market cap growth for tokenized real-world asset (RWA) funds, according to Token Terminal data published by the RWA Foundation. Over the 24 hours to Nov. 13, the market cap of tokenized funds on Stellar went up by $44.9 million, and the network surpassed both Ethereum and Solana.

Over the same period, the market cap of tokenized funds on Solana, Ethereum and zkSync Era increased by $29 million, $10.8 million and $3.5 million, respectively.

Stellar is currently the second-largest blockchain for tokenized funds after Ethereum, according to Token Terminal. Over the past year, the RWA market on Stellar has grown roughly sixfold and reached $4.67 billion, according to rwa.xyz. At press time, the price of XLM stands at $0.1476.

According to the Stellar Development Foundation, Stellar was designed with the requirements of banks and transfer agents in mind. In this context, the compliance tools are built into the base layer of the network, and an issuer can vet investors through trustlines, freeze accounts and claw back assets.

Transactions on Stellar settle in 3 to 5 seconds, and the fees on the network are measured in fractions of a cent. Besides, users can move funds to and from fiat currencies through local providers, which are called anchors on Stellar.

Franklin Templeton's BENJI money market fund has run on Stellar since 2021, and it was the first U.S. mutual fund on a public blockchain.

Today, Spiko, Ondo and WisdomTree are also building their own funds and tokenized U.S. Treasuries on Stellar. Spiko offers euro funds managed by Amundi, and Ondo has launched its USDY token on the network.

In May 2026, DTCC and the Stellar Development Foundation announced that the Depository Trust Company (DTC) will tokenize the assets it holds in custody on Stellar. According to DTCC, DTC-tokenized assets are expected to become available on the network in the first half of 2027.

On Nov. 12, DTCC also announced that it will connect its tokenization service to Solana in the second half of 2027.

#5191. The catch in crypto’s Anthropic IPO rush: lock up your money and you could still miss out

Anthropic IPO token buyers face uncertain share allocations, locked funds and fees of up to 12% ahead of its Nasdaq debut.

Crypto investors seeking Anthropic IPO tokens can commit money and still get a refund instead of an allocation.

Kraken, Bitget, and BigONE disclose subscription terms that make delivery dependent on available shares, while successful fills carry additional costs.

The issue became more immediate on Nov. 12 when BigONE opened indications of interest and warned users they could receive a full allocation, a partial allocation, or none. Kraken's Anthropic IPO access terms carry the same three possible outcomes, while Bitget says its commitment caps do not represent the shares it has secured.

Those warnings come ahead of Anthropic's expected Nov. 18 US-time pricing and Nov. 19 Nasdaq debut. Bloomberg News reported on Nov. 11, citing people familiar with the matter, that orders already exceeded the available shares multiple times.

The venues' terms make clear that money can become unavailable while an allocation is determined, and receiving tokens can mean paying above the offering price without acquiring direct shareholder rights.

Allocation decides what investors receive. Select a venue to see how money control, charges and expected delivery differ.

Kraken reserves funds. You can cancel free before the communicated cutoff; after it, the request becomes binding.

Bitget public commitments cannot be canceled. Funds stay locked; token delivery is expected before the regular U.S. session on IPO day.

The published VIP cutoff has passed. Commitments cannot be canceled; delivery is expected after the IPO and unallocated funds are expected back within hours of allocation confirmation, with delays possible.

BigONE uses cumulative subscription tiers and charges only on allocated shares. Full, partial or zero allocation remains possible.

Submitting money secures a place in the allocation process; the received tokens and refund depend on the result.

Anthropic's Nov. 10 preliminary prospectus offers 825 million Class A shares at an estimated $70 to $78 each. About 801.4 million are company shares and 23.6 million are being sold by existing holders, whose sale proceeds do not go to Anthropic.

Bloomberg News reported that the public offering could total up to $64 billion. A separate $26 billion Class N private placement would bring the combined amount to as much as $90 billion.

The published charges apply only to the amount allocated:

Kraken reserves money when a user submits interest and charges it only if an allocation is received, and reserved funds remain unavailable until allocation or release. Its cancellation right ends at a communicated cutoff, after which the submission becomes binding.

Supported stablecoin submissions are converted to dollars, and refunds arrive in dollars.

Bitget's restriction says users cannot cancel submitted commitments or trade, transfer, or withdraw locked funds. Its fee is charged by the partner fund, broker, or placement channel and is included in the commitment.

The venue expects remaining funds to be refunded within hours of allocation confirmation, while warning that arrival can be delayed and processing extended if issuance or allocation arrangements fail.

Bitget's published VIP window was scheduled to end Nov. 11, while its public window is scheduled to end at 08:00 UTC on the day before the IPO.

The higher VIP fee does not remove allocation uncertainty, and the expected three-to-five-working-day delivery means those tokens may arrive after the stock's first trading day.

BigONE's window runs through Nov. 18 at 12:00 UTC. Its notice promises refunds if the platform receives no allocation, plus 6% annualized compensation for the time each subscription's funds were committed.

Payments below 1 USDT per subscription are excluded, and the payment schedule will be announced separately.

Using the preliminary range's $78 upper endpoint as an illustration, a 5% surcharge yields an acquisition cost of $81.90 per unit, while a 12% surcharge yields $87.36.

Assuming a token tracks one share without price divergence, the underlying price would need to rise 5% or 12%, respectively, from $78 just to match those acquisition costs, before any later trading charges.

Kraken says unallocated funds return on listing day, BigONE expects ANTx delivery on Nov. 19, and Bitget targets rANT trading about an hour after Anthropic's Nasdaq IPO Cross, while its VIP delivery expectation extends several working days beyond the IPO.

#5190. Wall Street Trading Booms on Crypto Exchanges. Which Tokens Benefit?

Home » Trendsetter News » Wall Street Trading Booms on Crypto Exchanges. Which Tokens Benefit?

Crypto exchanges are seeing a surge in trading tied to traditional markets, but will token holders benefit most?

Crypto exchanges handled $3.16 trillion in trading tied to stocks, gold, oil and other traditional markets over the period tracked by research cited in a new Firehustle video episode.

The channel’s host, discussing crypto investment themes, argues that the important question is not how much trading these platforms attract, but whether that activity actually benefits HYPE, ONDO and INJ holders.

The figures, attributed to CoinMarketCap research covering 19 exchanges, describe trading exposure to traditional markets, not necessarily purchases of underlying shares. According to Fire Hustle, monthly volume climbed from roughly $100 billion in January to $800 billion in August, with stocks accounting for 62.3% of activity.

The expert identifies Hyperliquid as the closest to strengthening that connection. Trade.XYZ, which operates most of the platform’s traditional-market contracts, reportedly splits trading fees equally with Hyperliquid, whose share largely supports HYPE buybacks.

There is a catch: Trade.XYZ is operating with trading fees discounted by more than 90% to attract users. The YouTube video says those discounts are expected to shrink as markets mature, potentially increasing buyback funding, although higher fees could also change trading behavior.

ONDO presents a different problem. Fire Hustle says Ondo Finance surpassed $4 billion in total value locked, including more than $1.3 billion in tokenized stocks and ETFs, while ONDO holders currently receive no direct fee distributions, buybacks or burns.

A holder-led forum proposal would direct 20% of revenue toward token buybacks and burns, eventually rising to 40%. The host stresses that it is not an approved policy and says the team had not responded.

Crucially, the $4 billion figure represents assets deposited, not revenue available to distribute.

Injective already links application revenue to INJ buybacks and burns, according to the video. But its scale remains modest: the host cites roughly $215 million in traditional-market trading over 30 days and a largest buyback round of about $315,000.

The potential catalyst is Pineapple Prime, a planned mortgage-yield product.

More than $1 billion in mortgage records reportedly moved onto Injective, but the host makes an important distinction: those records are data, not yet money flowing through a live investment product.

In conclusion, these are three way different bets: higher fee capture, an unapproved governance change and a product launch.

None makes trading growth equivalent to token returns, especially when discounted fees, limited activity and concentrated infrastructure can interrupt the connection.

#5187. XRP Exchange Balances Hit Yearly High, but Long-Term Holders Stay Put

Home » Trendsetter News » XRP Exchange Balances Hit Yearly High, but Long-Term Holders Stay Put

XRP exchange balances have reached a one-year high, while the share of tokens untouched for over a year nears its annual peak.

XRP held on exchanges has reached a one-year high even as the share of coins untouched for more than a year approaches its own annual peak, according to figures cited by wealth-focused commentator Kamilah Stevenson.

Her latest video examines that split following a roughly 10% price decline, arguing that investors’ financial circumstances can matter as much as their market convictions.

Stevenson cites CryptoQuant data showing approximately 11.8 billion XRP on exchanges, the highest balance in a year. That puts more tokens within easy reach of trading, although exchange deposits alone do not establish that holders intend to sell.

Meanwhile, Glassnode figures cited in the video put the share of XRP unmoved for more than a year at roughly 56%, up from 51% in January. Stevenson also says XRP exchange-traded funds still hold about 1.19 billion tokens, despite a small outflow ending a reported 13-week inflow streak.

“Both groups saw the same price,” she says. “They reacted to it in completely opposite ways.”

The contrast is striking, but the metrics have limits. Coins remaining stationary demonstrate inactivity, not necessarily fresh buying or confidence, and neither measure establishes where XRP’s price goes next.

Dr. Stevenson identifies three recurring sources of selling pressure: leverage, investing money needed for near-term expenses, and entering a volatile market without a plan.

She cites roughly $25.7 million in XRP liquidations on Binance during a recent sell-off as an example of positions being closed regardless of investors’ intentions.

Her broader bullish case rests partly on institutional activity involving Ripple and its RLUSD stablecoin.

The YouTube video names Standard Chartered, Cross River Bank and DriveWealth among firms involved in custody, banking or settlement developments.

Those developments should not be treated as equivalent to demand for XRP itself. Nor does institutional infrastructure guarantee that token prices will recover.

The most durable point is about liquidity: cash reserves and manageable exposure reduce the likelihood that an unexpected bill or margin call dictates a sale.

Exchange balances may signal potential selling pressure across the market; they cannot reveal which holders can afford to wait.

#5186. Bitcoin’s futures pile has a problem: less cash to fuel a rebound

Bitcoin’s futures exposure meets weaker Treasury demand and thinning spot buying, leaving a rebound dependent on fresh demand.

DWF Labs' Martin Lee noted that Bitcoin futures open interest stood at 704,000 BTC this week, the highest since Sept. 24, while spot market liquidity continued to thin.

Meanwhile, the Treasury's $25 billion 30-year bond auction on Nov. 12 drew a 2.36 bid-to-cover ratio, down from 2.54 in October, and cleared at 5.441% against a 5.437% when-issued yield, a 0.4-basis-point tail.

The 10-year sale two days earlier showed a sharper slide, with bid-to-cover at 2.46 against 2.77 in October.

The 10-year cleared at 5.02%, with indirect bidders taking about 61.2% of competitive awards versus 80.3% in October, and dealers taking 9.8% versus 2.5%. The 3-year sale on Nov. 9 drew 2.53 against 2.62.

The 30-year result sits within the range of recent sales, since August's new issue drew 2.39. The Treasury said on Nov. 4 that demand for short-term bills remained strong, so the auctions show weaker appetite for duration, and a retreat from US debt would be a larger claim.

Treasury expects $618 billion of privately held net borrowing in October through December and $800 billion in January through March. The $125 billion in 3-, 10-, and 30-year refunding sales raises about $28 billion in new cash.

Two-year yields near 4.835% and 10-year yields near 5.068% on Nov. 12 make cash and government debt more competitive with Bitcoin.

The 10-year fell 0.31, compared with 0.18 for the 30-year and 0.09 for the 3-year. October’s 10- and 30-year sales reopened existing securities, while November’s sales were new issues.

Source: TreasuryDirect - Oct. 6, 3-year note · TreasuryDirect - Oct. 7, 10-year note reopening · TreasuryDirect - Oct. 8, 30-year bond reopening · TreasuryDirect - Nov. 9, 3-year note · TreasuryDirect - Nov. 10, 10-year note · TreasuryDirect - Nov. 12, 30-year bond

Lee describes dollar-debasement demand and broader risk-on flows as two supports for Bitcoin in past rallies. Both helped in the 2020 to 2022 cycle, and in August the debasement narrative let Bitcoin hold up while AI stocks corrected.

“The limitation is that debasement alone rarely sustains a rally when the broader market is risk-off.”

He sees little chance of liquidity rotating into crypto until uncertainty from the midterms and a near-certain December hike clears. Adoption continues, with Airwallex launching its own chain and the NYSE advancing a tokenized stock platform.

Lee said Bitcoin options open interest recovered to 447,000 BTC from a dip between Nov. 6 and Nov. 9, though it remains 5% to 10% below October. Bitcoin's futures open interest is about 12% below its 2026 high, while Ethereum's is down about 30% since May and Solana's about 23% since June.

At an illustrative $72,000, 704,000 BTC equals about $51 billion of gross notional. Open interest counts outstanding contracts with a buyer and a seller on each, so it mixes long bets, short bets and hedges, and it describes positioning, a measure separate from fresh capital.

Glassnode noted on Nov. 11 that open interest had rebuilt toward September levels while Bitcoin sat about 15% below its September high, a pattern consistent with traders adding shorts during the decline.

Futures can amplify a rebound through short covering or a decline through forced closures, and both routes depend on spot liquidity.

Glassnode’s Nov. 11 analysis found resting bids within 5% of price outweighing asks on Binance and Coinbase since Nov. 5, with the largest concentration between $68,000 and $72,500.

Wallets holding 100 to 1,000 BTC and 1,000 to 10,000 BTC are accumulating, and other cohorts are distributing. A resting bid shows willingness to buy, and whether purchases follow depends on the bid surviving, since bids can be pulled or overwhelmed.

Daily net flows across the US spot Bitcoin ETFs , showing seven of eight sessions with net outflows.

Source: Farside Investors — Bitcoin ETF Flow, daily fund totals

“We've seen outflows accelerate at the bottoms and inflows accelerate at the tops.”

DWF Labs' Oct. 22 study of 694 trading days found ETF flows correlated 0.54 with Bitcoin's prior five-day return and 0.03 with its next five-day return. Flows turned negative on the low day in seven of eight qualifying selloffs and positive on the peak day in seven of eight tops.

About 20% of ETF buying was historically tied to CME short hedges.

Glassnode puts the True Market Mean near $77,500, a modeled six-month liquidation concentration at $59,500 to $62,600, a June low near $58,500 and a short-liquidation cluster near $87,500.

A recovery would have stronger backing if buyers absorb selling in the $68,000 to $72,500 band, Bitcoin reclaims $75,600 and $77,500, the Coinbase premium turns positive and stablecoin supply resumes growing. That combination could make futures positioning fuel for a rebound.

If bids give way while holder profitability erodes and stablecoin supply keeps contracting, leveraged positions could amplify a decline. Glassnode’s modeled $59,500 to $62,600 zone marks a possible area of liquidation pressure, not a price target.

#5185. TRON, Tether and Chainalysis launch task force as crypto hacks hit $8.78B

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

On the 12th of November, TRON, Tether, and blockchain intelligence firm Chainalysis jointly launched the Digital Crime Task Force (DCTF), an initiative aimed at identifying and disrupting illicit financial activities involving Tether’s USDT stablecoin on the TRON blockchain.

In this plan, TRON will contribute its blockchain network expertise, and Tether will provide support as the issuer of USDT. Meanwhile, Chainalysis will bring its blockchain intelligence, investigative expertise, and AI-powered monitoring tools.

One of the major reasons behind the initiative is the growing sophistication of crypto-related financial crime. According to Chainalysis, AI-enabled scam operations were 4.5x more profitable than traditional scams in 2025. Meanwhile, impersonation scams increased by more than 1,400% year over year.

DefiLlama further reported that the crypto industry recorded $8.78 billion across 328 hacks in 2026 so far. This is the highest annual loss recorded in its database. In fact, the five biggest hacks together contributed more than 85% of the overall losses.

Interestingly, the number of attacks increased around 2.7 times compared to 2025, while the median loss declined from $1.07 million to $510,000. This suggests that hackers are carrying out more frequent attacks, although most incidents involve relatively smaller amounts.

Seeing this rise, the organizations believe that traditional approaches, which often depend on victims reporting crimes or investigators identifying suspicious funds, are no longer sufficient. Instead, they want to identify potential threats before criminals can move their funds.

Remarking on the same, Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said,

Criminals are using AI to move faster than ever, and waiting for a victim to report a crime is no longer good enough

This remark comes as Tether has already frozen more than $7 billion linked to illicit activities while working with over 360 law enforcement agencies across 73 countries.

That said, the new task force will therefore be built on these efforts by focusing on proactive investigations and faster coordination. It will also accept tips and asset-freezing requests directly from law enforcement agencies.

Needless to say, the DCTF will investigate several categories of financial crime, including investment and romance scams, stolen funds, cryptocurrency hacks, terrorist financing, North Korean cyber operations, and much more.

This coincided with the FBI recently launching ‘Operation Blackout,’ a coordinated international crackdown targeting scam compounds across Southeast Asia, Africa, and the Middle East that defraud American citizens through fake investment platforms and online impersonation.

Meanwhile, ACAMS has partnered with blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis to strengthen cryptocurrency anti-financial crime training through an updated CCAS certification.

#5183. What Are Solana Privacy Rings? Inside Helius’ Privacy Protocol for Solana

Every transaction on Solana is public by default. Anyone can look up a wallet address and see its balance, what it has sent and received, and when. That transparency is useful for verifying the network, but a problem for anyone who doesn't want their finances on display: a business paying salaries, a trader building a position, or an individual who simply doesn't want strangers seeing their savings.

Rings are programmable, onchain environments for encrypting money, markets, and finance - without ever leaving Solana

Now live on mainnet. pic.twitter.com/ezCIUCjcbI

Rings support SOL and other tokens on Solana, including SPL and Token-2022 tokens. Users keep custody of their funds throughout, since every transaction needs the owner's signature.

Crucially, the private balances live on the same network as everything else. Private transactions execute directly on Solana and encrypted data is stored on Solana's ledger, with no separate layer-2 network or sequencer in between. That means private balances sit alongside the same stablecoins, tokenized assets and DeFi liquidity as public ones.

Each private transfer comes with a zero-knowledge proof, a piece of cryptography that lets the network confirm the transfer is valid, for example that the sender actually had the funds, without revealing the numbers involved. Rings use a type of zero-knowledge proof called a Groth16 zk-SNARK, which Helius says can be generated in tens of milliseconds, either by a service provider or on the user's own device. Each private transfer settles in a single Solana transaction.

Users read their own encrypted balances with a viewing key. They can decrypt their balance locally, or let a service provider decrypt it and serve it to them, and they can share a key for a single transaction with an auditor or counterparty without exposing the rest of their history.

Moving funds into a Ring from an ordinary public wallet, or back out again, is visible onchain, including the asset and amount. But users who on-ramp from fiat currency straight into a private balance, through a supported provider, keep the asset and amount hidden from the start, according to Helius.

Because Custom Rings interoperate with the default Ring, regulated firms can keep their activity confidential from the market while still sharing the same liquidity as everyone else.

Private transfers are just the start. Solana programs can hold encrypted balances in private escrows and release them when set conditions are met, opening the way for:

At launch, Decrypt, mining and staking app ORE and cross-chain service Aurora Intents were using the default Ring, while Backpack, DFlow, Jupiter, Squads and Titan were among the teams working on integrations.

Helius says the core programs and zero-knowledge circuits have been audited by security firms Certora, OtterSec and ZK Security. Engineers from the Solana Foundation, Blueshift, Zcash and other teams took part in the "trusted setup," the one-off ceremony that generates the parameters the proofs rely on.

The code is open source, published on GitHub under the Apache 2.0 license, so anyone can inspect how it works.

Formal verification, a mathematical check that the circuits behave exactly as intended, is still underway and expected to finish by the end of 2026. Solana's own documentation currently describes Rings as being in beta.

#5182. The cost of a $70,000 Bitcoin hedge more than doubled in a day

Captured Deribit data show a November 27 put rising 127.6% between two BTC-denominated trades, even as its reported implied volatility fell.

A Bitcoin hedge using a put with a $70,000 strike more than doubled in BTC terms between November 12 and 13, even as its reported implied volatility fell. On November 13, Deribit's broad volatility gauge hovered near 40, showing why a calm index alone cannot reveal the cost of protecting a holding.

Deribit observations from November 12–13 show its November 27 $70,000 put traded at 0.0145 BTC at 11:51 UTC on November 12 and 0.033 BTC at 10:15 UTC on November 13, an increase of 127.6% in BTC terms. Yet the implied volatility reported for those executions fell from 38.97% to 37.67%.

Bitcoin's index price at the two trades fell from $72,805.71 to $69,320.08, taking it from above the fixed strike to below it. A put provides protection against a fall below that strike at expiry. As Bitcoin falls, that fixed protection can become more valuable even without higher implied volatility.

For a new buyer at 10:40:51 UTC on November 13, the contract's order book showed a 0.0325 BTC bid and a 0.0335 BTC ask. With the index at $69,245.85, that ask equaled about $2,319.74 for one contract before fees. The 127.6% increase compares executed BTC prices, rather than measuring a change in executable asks.

A protective put's premium is the price of protection at a specified strike and expiry. Implied volatility is one component of that price. The underlying price, the strike, the forward price and the time remaining also matter. CryptoSlate’s crypto options platform comparison explains how contract design, settlement and execution costs differ across venues.

The two executions do not isolate how much of the premium change came from each pricing input. The contract also had less time remaining at the second trade.

The currency of the quote adds another difference. Deribit's inverse Bitcoin options are priced in BTC, and one contract represents one BTC. Converting each selected trade at its own contemporaneous index gives about $1,055.68 on November 12 and $2,287.56 on November 13. The increase in those dollar equivalents was 116.7%, smaller than the BTC-denominated increase.

The $70,000 strike also does not promise a $70,000 net sale price. The buyer pays the BTC premium upfront, and trading fees, delivery fees, currency conversion and the settlement reference affect the net result. At expiry, an in-the-money inverse put settles through an immediately settling inverse futures contract into BTC, with the economic result of cash settlement. An out-of-the-money put expires worthless.

Thanks for signing up to The Catalyst. Look out for your first daily email. If you already receive it, you’re all set.

The Nov. 27 $70,000 put cost more in BTC between executions on Nov. 12 and 13, even as its reported trade IV fell.

A fixed-strike put can cost more as Bitcoin falls, without a rise in its implied volatility.

Different-sized executions, not matched executable bid/ask quotes. Same expiry, different time remaining and moneyness. IV is reported for each trade, not DVOL. Prices exclude fees; the $70,000 strike is not a net sale-price guarantee.

Two timestamped executions: Nov. 12 2026 11:51:01 UTC and Nov. 13 10:15:10 UTC. Index dots share a linear USD scale; premiums use a zero-based 0–0.04 BTC scale. Values reported by Deribit. No path, interpolation or causal decomposition is inferred.

Different-sized executions, not matched executable bid/ask quotes. Same expiry, different time remaining and moneyness. IV is reported for each trade, not DVOL. Prices exclude fees; the $70,000 strike is not a net sale-price guarantee.

Deribit defines DVOL as forward-looking, annualized implied volatility over 30 days, assembled across strikes and expiries. The November 27 put had roughly 14 days remaining. One broad index and one shorter-dated contract therefore describe different exposures.

The completed November 13 hourly buckets from 00:00 through 09:00 UTC recorded intrahour lows and highs spanning 39.03 to 41.58. The 09:00 bucket closed at 39.93; the 10:00 bucket was still incomplete when captured at 10:40 UTC.

A November 13 analysis by The Daily Digits on CryptoQuant supplies historical context. It reports DVOL of 40.77 against a median of 77.8 across 290 daily closes since March 2021 when Bitcoin was at least 17.4% below its rolling 30-day closing high. Its median for qualifying 2026 observations was 49.9, a closer current-year benchmark.

Those daily observations can overlap within a single selloff. They are not 290 independent crises, and the study does not give an exact intraday timestamp tying its reading to the put quotes. The comparison establishes the study's historical framing, rather than a fair price for this hedge.

October's Producer Price Index was scheduled for November 13 at 08:30 Eastern, or 13:30 UTC, after these market observations. The scheduled inflation release provides a clear checkpoint for observing any repricing; it does not establish a cause for the earlier move.

A useful before-and-after comparison would track the same contract's bid, ask and implied volatility alongside its forward price and time remaining, then examine pricing across strikes. That separates a change in the cost of buying protection from a change in volatility pricing more clearly than DVOL alone.

For a holder, the immediate consequence is already visible: maintaining a Bitcoin hedge at a fixed dollar strike can become more expensive as Bitcoin falls, even while the broad volatility gauge remains subdued.

#5181. Strategy Sends Crucial Message on Bitcoin's Quantum Security

Strategy, the world's largest corporate Bitcoin (BTC) holder, has sent an important message regarding Bitcoin’s future resistance to quantum computing attacks.

The company, which was co-founded by renowned Bitcoin champion Michael Saylor, recently posted on X that the Bitcoin network can implement new security measures as and when they are needed.

“Quantum-resistant upgrades can be adopted if & when it's needed,” wrote Strategy.

These comments come at a time when the crypto industry is debating whether the rise of quantum computing could, in the long run, threaten Bitcoin’s cryptographic security.

Given that Bitcoin leverages elliptic curve cryptography for transaction security, quantum computing could pose a significant threat to Bitcoin.

A sufficiently powerful quantum computer has the potential to reverse-engineer private keys from exposed public keys. This could give attackers access to the Bitcoin holdings associated with those keys.

At this point, there is no known publicly available quantum computer that can successfully break Bitcoin’s cryptography in this manner.

While speaking at the World Bank in Washington in October, Saylor said that the Bitcoin network would be able to defend itself against any realistic quantum computing threat by coming together and upgrading the software.

Saylor estimated that such an upgrade would take about 90 days once a worldwide consensus is reached on the need for quantum-resistant cryptography.

Saylor also warned against the hasty introduction of new cryptography. He reasoned that more complex security measures may themselves introduce weaknesses.

However, the 90-day estimate has come under scrutiny because such a network-wide shift would involve developers agreeing on technical changes and Bitcoin users moving their funds to new, secure addresses.

Interestingly, Strategy has also initiated efforts aimed at research and development for Bitcoin’s long-term security.

In July, Strategy was part of a group of seven major financial institutions and crypto companies, including BlackRock and Coinbase, that formed the Bitcoin Security Consortium.

The Bitcoin Security Consortium has committed $15 million over three years. One of the areas of focus of the consortium is post-quantum cryptography.

In fact, Bitcoin developers are already working on ways to address the quantum computing issue.

One of the most prominent proposals is Bitcoin Improvement Proposal 360 (BIP-360). This BIP introduces a new type of transaction output, Pay-to-Merkle-Root (P2MR).

On the 13th of November, Arthur Hayes announced that Flop Labs will launch its testnet and airdrop. The AI-compute blockchain has a launch date for November 24 and a pitch revolving around “food for your AI agent.”

In a nutshell, FLOP is a token that AI agents spend on inference and memory storage, and miners can earn it by offering up GPU processors.

Hayes became CEO of Flop Labs in August 2026, after a public bet against the AI bubble, that these debt-funded data centers will crash and leave behind an abundance of GPUs.

Flop Labs runs on “proof of useful inference”: miners supply GPUs to process “AI inference” requests, the validators confirm the delivery, and agents spend FLOP tokens for their expenses.

This case was further strengthened on the 9th of November, when a developer demonstrated FLOP mining on an Nvidia RTX 5080.

Hayes confirmed that this was the long-term goal of FLOP, stating,

Mining FLOP isn’t just for folks with access to the highest spec GPUs. We specially want retail users to mine with consumer graphics cards, Mac Mini’s, etc.

Notably, Hayes confirmed that no token has been created yet. However, in August he stated that there is no presale, no memecoin, and no FLOP token, only,

Still, the biggest criticism is that Flop Labs still lacks a full whitepaper and verification details.

In the past, crypto sleuth ZachXBT has publicly accused Hayes of promoting tokens like Worldcoin [WLD], Near Protocol [NEAR], Hyperliquid [HYPE], and Zcash [ZEC] before selling into the demand that his posts created. Hayes did not deny the trades; he admitted,

I sold to a willing seller at a price… I just happened to call it right this time as it regards to my trading goals.

So, it’s difficult to believe Hayes when he tells his 800K followers that FLOP is the future of agent commerce.

The 24th of November will bring with it a testnet and an airdrop. However, Flop Labs and Arthur Hayes still have a ways to go before they can confirm that Hayes’ anti-bubble bet is real.

#5179. Ripple Prime CEO Steps Down Ahead Of XRP Expansion

Home » Ripple (XRP) » Ripple Prime CEO Steps Down Ahead Of XRP Expansion

XRP’s financial utility goes way beyond cross-border operations: leadership shift shakes Ripple’s prominent brokerage arm.

Ripple’s Ripple Prime institutional crypto brokerage platform is witnessing a major change. Ripple Prime founder Marc Asch is going to leave the position at year-end as Noel Kimmel assumes leadership.

Noel Kimmel, already serving as Vice President of Ripple Prime, will assume leadership of the business and their team within Ripple Labs. This marks Ripple Prime’s transition from a regular custody & brokerage platform to major-scale financial services & infrastructure provider.

Marc Asch founded Hidden Road back in 2018, instantly becoming the growing brokerage’s CEO. The company offered a wide variety of digital-asset powered services, including foreign exchange, derivatives and fixed income. Ripple made a deal to acquire the platform in 2025.

Since the massive acquisition, Ripple Labs expanded the newly-acquired subsidiary’s business towards leveraged ETF financing. The branch even processed $13 trillion in payments during 2025, but the vague regulations kept all of that trading action outside of crypto’s boundaries.

Ripple Prime founder Marc Asch is stepping down at year end, per CoinDesk, with Noel Kimmel taking over the prime brokerage Ripple bought for $1.25B in 2025. Founders leaving a year after a sale is normal. The test is whether institutions keep growing there. Red flag or nothing?

Right now, Ripple Prime serves over 300 institutions worldwide. The freshly-appointed CEO Noel Kimmel was already deeply involved in this expansion. He previously represented Ripple Prime in its $200 million financing agreement, designed to raise institutional margin capacity.

The brokerage platform went on to introduce equity-linked derivatives and financing for Ripple’s institutional customers. Another key milestone was the deal with Brevan Howard, an accounting company looking after $35 billion in assets under management (AUM) for clearing services.

Presently, XRP coin’s trading dangerously close to the psychological $1 level on November 13, 2026. This extends a sharp dip as Bitcoin (BTC) falls below $68,000 and with the crypto ETF market taking a multi-billion dollar hit on Friday. The $0.99 support zone comes into play now.

#5178. Nakamoto Sells More Bitcoin (BTC)

As per its latest quarterly financials, David Bailey's Bitcoin treasury firm Nakamoto Inc. (NASDAQ: NAKA) has sold an additional 184 BTC from its Bitcoin stash.

Nakamoto Inc., a firm that built its corporate strategy around Bitcoin, held a total of 4,283 BTC as of Sept. 30. The figure is down from 4,467 BTC at the end of June.

Bitcoin Treasuries data shows that Nakamoto Inc. sold 184 BTC in the third quarter of 2026. The firm now has a total of 4,283 BTC in its Bitcoin stash. Nakamoto currently sits in 21st place on the Bitcoin 100 corporate treasury rankings.

The recent company filing indicates that Nakamoto Inc. generated around $13.2 million in proceeds from digital asset sales in the third quarter. However, the filing does not appear to specify whether the 184 BTC were sold in a single transaction.

Nakamoto currently holds approximately $357.9 million worth of Bitcoin despite selling more BTC in the latest period.

This is not the first time in 2026 that David Bailey's firm has reduced its Bitcoin stash.

In March, Nakamoto Inc. sold around 284 BTC worth $20 million to meet working capital needs and fund operations following its acquisitions of BTC Inc. and UTXO Management.

Nakamoto sold its BTC at an average price of around $70,422 per Bitcoin. That was far less than its original Bitcoin purchase price.

In the first quarter, Nakamoto Inc. also received a premium of around 43 BTC from its derivatives strategies before selling around 40 BTC.

Nakamoto Inc. also sold a large chunk of Bitcoin in June.

The company sold around 600 BTC for 35.6 million USDT, as per the company's second-quarter financials.

Combined with proceeds from certain Bitcoin derivative positions, the company generated around $48 million from those transactions.

Nakamoto Inc. used $45 million of that sum to partially repay its Bitcoin-backed loan from cryptocurrency exchange Kraken, reducing its principal amount from 210 million USDT to 165 million USDT.

The recent Bitcoin sell-off comes as Nakamoto continues working to meet its substantial debt obligations while expanding its business operations.

It had roughly 3,030 BTC pledged as collateral for debt as of Sept. 30. That left 1,253 BTC unpledged.

On Nov. 11, Nakamoto Inc. extended the maturity of a 60 million USDT loan from Kraken by one year. The company moved the loan maturity date from December 2026 to December 2027. Nakamoto currently has no remaining principal maturities in 2026.

#5177. How TSMC’s employee data leak raises questions over cloud security
